Assume Countable Choice for the smooth tangent-bundle and time-orientation conventions of the Lorentzian suppliers. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$. A **closed spacelike two-surface** is a nonempty smooth embedded two-manifold $S\subset M$ that is compact without boundary. Let $\iota:S\hookrightarrow M$ be the inclusion and let its induced metric be $q:=\iota^*g$; require $q$ to be positive definite. Its normal bundle is $\mathcal NS=(TS)^\perp$. Work on an open set $U\subseteq S$ carrying a smooth ordered pair of future null normal fields $\ell,k$ with $g(\ell,\ell)=g(k,k)=0$ and $g(\ell,k)=-2$; such pairs exist locally by the preceding lemma. No global pair is part of the definition unless one is explicitly supplied.

For tangent fields $X,Y$ on $U$, define the null second fundamental form, expansion and shear by
$$\chi_\ell(X,Y):=g(\nabla_X\ell,Y),\qquad \theta_\ell:=\operatorname{tr}_q\chi_\ell,\qquad \sigma_\ell:=\chi_\ell-\frac{\theta_\ell}{2}q.$$
Here $\nabla$ is the metric-selected connection; its derivative of a section along $S$ means the pullback connection, equivalently the derivative of any smooth ambient extension along tangent directions. The preceding lemma establishes extension independence, symmetry of $\chi_\ell$, and positive definiteness of the screen metric. A **normal-frame boost** is the change $\ell\mapsto e^f\ell$, $k\mapsto e^{-f}k$ for a smooth real function $f$ on $U$. It leaves $q$ fixed; $\chi_\ell,\theta_\ell,\sigma_\ell$ scale by $e^f$.

A **null geodesic hypersurface congruence from $U$** along the chosen initial normal field $\ell$ is a smooth map $F:U\times J\to M$, where $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ is a nonempty open interval containing $0$, such that $F(p,0)=p$ and $\partial_\lambda F(p,0)=\ell_p$ for every $p\in U$, each curve $\gamma_p(\lambda):=F(p,\lambda)$ is future-directed and null, and its tangent $\ell:=\partial_\lambda F$ obeys the affine geodesic equation
$$D_\lambda\ell=0$$
along every curve $\gamma_p$; here $D_\lambda$ is the covariant derivative along a curve from [[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]. For each $p\in U$, let $J_{\mathrm{reg}}(p)$ be the connected component containing $0$ of the parameter values for which $d(F_\lambda)_p:T_pU\to T_{F(p,\lambda)}M$ is injective and the pullback form $(X,Y)\mapsto g(d(F_\lambda)_pX,d(F_\lambda)_pY)$ is positive definite on $T_pU$. Require, for every $\lambda\in J$, that its variation directions satisfy
$$g_{F(p,\lambda)}\bigl(\ell(p,\lambda),dF_{(p,\lambda)}(X,0)\bigr)=0\qquad(X\in T_pU).$$
Thus its variation directions are orthogonal to $\ell$. For $\lambda\in J_{\mathrm{reg}}(p)$, the map $F$ has rank three locally near $(p,\lambda)$: its two section directions are spacelike and orthogonal to the nonzero null vector $\ell$. Its local image is a null hypersurface, with tangent space $\ell^\perp$ and induced radical $\mathbb R\ell$, as in [[lem-gr-fx-null-normal-plane-and-screen]]. The parameter $\lambda$ is affine. On each section in $J_{\mathrm{reg}}$, the **screen** is $\mathscr S=\ell^\perp/\mathbb R\ell$ with metric $\bar q([X],[Y])=g(X,Y)$; it is the positive two-dimensional quotient, identified isometrically with the tangent plane of that section by projection. The induced form on the full null hypersurface has radical $\mathbb R\ell$ and has no inverse. All traces and inverses in this definition are taken on the screen.

All screen bundles associated with this congruence are understood as bundles over the parameter domain $U\times J$: the notation $\mathscr S_{F(p,\lambda)}$ denotes the branch determined by $(p,\lambda)$, so self-intersections do not identify distinct screen fibers. For each $\lambda\in J$, the screen Jacobi map $A_\lambda:T_pS\to\mathscr S_{F(p,\lambda)}$ sends $X$ to the screen class of the variation field $J_X(\lambda):=dF_{(p,\lambda)}(X,0)$; it is invertible for $\lambda\in J_{\mathrm{reg}}(p)$. A **focal instant** is a positive parameter in $J$ where $A_\lambda$ loses rank; the **first focal instant**, if it exists, is the least such parameter after $0$. Along an affine generator the screen derivative is $\mathcal D_\ell[X]:=[D_\ell X]$; it is independent of the representative, by the preceding lemma. On $J_{\mathrm{reg}}$, the derivative $A_\lambda'$ is taken using $\mathcal D_\ell$, and the **optical endomorphism** is $B_\lambda:=A_\lambda'A_\lambda^{-1}$. Its **optical expansion** is $\theta:=\operatorname{tr}B$, and its **optical shear** is $\sigma:=B-\frac12\theta\,\mathrm{id}_{\mathscr S}$. Since the congruence is normal to a null hypersurface, $B$ is self-adjoint. Its antisymmetric part $\omega:=(B-B^*)/2$, called the twist, therefore vanishes. At $\lambda=0$, $B$ is the endomorphism $q^{-1}\chi_\ell$ and these optical quantities agree with $\theta_\ell,\sigma_\ell$.

No orientation of $M$, $S$, or the screen is required for these constructions. Indeed, if two orthonormal screen frames are related by a real $2\times2$ matrix $O$ with $O^{\mathsf T}O=I_2$, then the endomorphism matrices obey $\widehat B=O^{-1}BO$ and $\widehat\sigma=O^{-1}\sigma O$. Cyclicity of the matrix trace gives $\operatorname{tr}\widehat B=\operatorname{tr}B$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\widehat\sigma^2)=\operatorname{tr}(\sigma^2)=|\sigma|_{\bar q}^2$; the last equality follows by summing the squared entries of the symmetric shear matrix in an orthonormal frame. This includes $\det O=-1$. The screen inner products and the rank of $A_\lambda$ are likewise invariant under changes of frame, so neither the index-form contractions nor the focal condition uses a signed screen area form. The preceding lemma constructs normal pairs using the supplied time orientation and only a local spacelike complement; changing the complement's sign interchanges the two future null rays. No global ordered pair follows. If an orientation is additionally supplied, the same formulas apply on that oriented subclass.

Assume Countable Choice for the Lorentzian supplier conventions. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, let $S$ be a smooth spacelike two-surface, and let $F:U\times J\to M$ be a smooth null geodesic hypersurface congruence from an open section $U\subseteq S$, as defined in [[def-gr-fx-null-screen-geometry]]. Write $\ell=\partial_\lambda F$ and fix $p\in U$. Before the first focal instant let $A_\lambda:T_pS\to\mathscr S_{F(p,\lambda)}$ be the screen Jacobi map, $B=A'A^{-1}$ the optical endomorphism, $\theta=\operatorname{tr}B$ its expansion, and $\sigma=B-\frac12\theta\,\mathrm{id}$ its shear. Let $\operatorname{Ric}$ be the Ricci tensor in [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]. Then, along the generator $\gamma(\lambda)=F(p,\lambda)$ and before the first focal instant,
$$\frac{d\theta}{d\lambda}=-\frac{\theta^2}{2}-|\sigma|_{\bar q}^2-\operatorname{Ric}(\ell,\ell).$$
If $\operatorname{Ric}(\ell,\ell)\ge0$ along the generator and $\theta(0)<0$, then a first focal instant occurs by affine parameter
$$\lambda_*=\frac{2}{|\theta(0)|},$$
provided the smooth congruence and generator are defined through $\lambda_*$. Here a focal instant means that the screen Jacobi map loses rank; the conclusion is local along this generator and asserts no curvature singularity.

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice, as required by the supplied
causal-curve and push-up results. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold. Let $S$ be a smooth embedded two-manifold without
boundary whose induced metric $q:=g|_{TS}$ is positive definite, and let
$p\in S$. Choose an open neighborhood $U\subseteq S$ of $p$ and a smooth
future null normal field $\ell$ along $U$, so
$g(\ell_q,Y)=0$ for every $q\in U$ and $Y\in T_qS$.
Let $\gamma:[0,L_1]\to M$ be smooth up to its endpoints, with
$$\gamma(0)=p,\qquad \dot\gamma(0)=\ell_p,\qquad g(\dot\gamma,\dot\gamma)=0,\qquad g(\dot\gamma,N)<0,\qquad D_\lambda\dot\gamma=0.$$
Here $D_\lambda$ is covariant differentiation along the curve. Put
$\chi_\ell(X,Y):=g(\nabla_X\ell,Y)$ as in
[[def-gr-fx-null-screen-geometry]], and set $B_0:T_pS\to T_pS$ by
$q(B_0X,Y)=\chi_\ell(X,Y)$ for all $X,Y\in T_pS$.
The screen along $\gamma$ is
$$\mathscr S_\lambda:=\dot\gamma(\lambda)^\perp/\mathbb R\dot\gamma(\lambda),$$
with its positive metric and screen derivative $\mathcal D_\lambda$ from
[[def-gr-fx-null-screen-geometry]]. Define
$$\mathcal R_\lambda[X]:=[R(X,\dot\gamma)\dot\gamma].$$
A **normal screen Jacobi field** is a smooth section $J$ of $\mathscr S$ that
satisfies $\mathcal D_\lambda^2J+\mathcal R_\lambda J=0$ and the initial
conditions $J(0)=[X]$, $\mathcal D_\lambda J(0)=B_0X$ for some
$X\in T_pS$. A **focal instant** $\lambda_0\in(0,L_1]$ is a parameter at
which such a field with $X\ne0$ has $J(\lambda_0)=0$.

Put $I^+(S):=\bigcup_{p\in S}I^+(p)$,
$J^+(S):=\bigcup_{p\in S}J^+(p)$, and
$E^+(S):=J^+(S)\setminus I^+(S)$, using the causal-reachability conventions
of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]].

If $\lambda_0$ is a focal instant, there is $\varepsilon>0$ such that
$$\gamma(\lambda)\in I^+(S)\qquad (\lambda_0<\lambda<\lambda_0+\varepsilon).$$
Consequently, no point on this portion of the generator belongs to
$E^+(S)$. The conclusion is local along the generator and does not assert
geodesic incompleteness or curvature blow-up. In an SI interpretation take
$x^0=ct$ and $\lambda$ in metres; the proof itself is independent of units.

derivations.claim:
On $S$, $q=R^2d\Omega^2$. For tangent $X,Y$, flat-space differentiation
gives $\nabla_X\partial_r=X/R$ and $\nabla_X\partial_t=0$. Therefore
$\chi_\ell=q/R$ and $\chi_k=-q/R$, and since the screen dimension is two,
$\theta_\ell=2/R$ and $\theta_k=-2/R$. Direct inner products give
$g(\ell,\ell)=g(k,k)=0$ and $g(\ell,k)=-1-1=-2$; both fields are future
because their $t$ components are $1$.

In Cartesian coordinates the inward geodesic is
$\gamma_\omega(\lambda)=(\lambda,(R-\lambda)\omega)$. Varying $\omega$ in a
tangent direction $X\in T_{R\omega}(R\mathbb S^2)$ gives the Jacobi field
$J_X(\lambda)=(1-\lambda/R)X$. Its screen map is therefore
$A_\lambda=(1-\lambda/R)\operatorname{id}$ for $0\le\lambda<R$, with first
rank loss at $R$. Hence $B=-\operatorname{id}/(R-\lambda)$,
$\theta=-2/(R-\lambda)$, $\sigma=0$, and $\operatorname{Ric}=0$. Differentiating
$\theta$ verifies the equation in [F2], and
$2/|\theta(0)|=2/(2/R)=R$, so the comparison bound is sharp.

Fix $R<\lambda<3R$. The point $p_-= (0,-R\omega)\in S$ and
$q_\lambda=\gamma_\omega(\lambda)$ have time separation $\lambda$ and spatial
separation
$$|(R-\lambda)\omega-(-R\omega)|=|2R-\lambda|<\lambda.$$
The straight segment from $p_-$ to $q_\lambda$ is future timelike because
its time component is positive and its squared interval is
$-\lambda^2+(2R-\lambda)^2<0$. Thus $q_\lambda\in I^+(S)$. This agrees with
[F3] for parameters sufficiently close to $R$; the displayed segment proves
the stronger stated range $R<\lambda<3R$ directly.

Assume Countable Choice for the smooth tangent-bundle and time-orientation conventions of the Lorentzian suppliers. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$. A **closed spacelike two-surface** is a nonempty smooth embedded two-manifold $S\subset M$ that is compact without boundary. Let $\iota:S\hookrightarrow M$ be the inclusion and let its induced metric be $q:=\iota^*g$; require $q$ to be positive definite. Its normal bundle is $\mathcal NS=(TS)^\perp$. Work on an open set $U\subseteq S$ carrying a smooth ordered pair of future null normal fields $\ell,k$ with $g(\ell,\ell)=g(k,k)=0$ and $g(\ell,k)=-2$; such pairs exist locally by the preceding lemma. No global pair is part of the definition unless one is explicitly supplied.

For tangent fields $X,Y$ on $U$, define the null second fundamental form, expansion and shear by
$$\chi_\ell(X,Y):=g(\nabla_X\ell,Y),\qquad \theta_\ell:=\operatorname{tr}_q\chi_\ell,\qquad \sigma_\ell:=\chi_\ell-\frac{\theta_\ell}{2}q.$$
Here $\nabla$ is the metric-selected connection; its derivative of a section along $S$ means the pullback connection, equivalently the derivative of any smooth ambient extension along tangent directions. The preceding lemma establishes extension independence, symmetry of $\chi_\ell$, and positive definiteness of the screen metric. A **normal-frame boost** is the change $\ell\mapsto e^f\ell$, $k\mapsto e^{-f}k$ for a smooth real function $f$ on $U$. It leaves $q$ fixed; $\chi_\ell,\theta_\ell,\sigma_\ell$ scale by $e^f$.

A **null geodesic hypersurface congruence from $U$** along the chosen initial normal field $\ell$ is a smooth map $F:U\times J\to M$, where $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ is a nonempty open interval containing $0$, such that $F(p,0)=p$ and $\partial_\lambda F(p,0)=\ell_p$ for every $p\in U$, each curve $\gamma_p(\lambda):=F(p,\lambda)$ is future-directed and null, and its tangent $\ell:=\partial_\lambda F$ obeys the affine geodesic equation
$$D_\lambda\ell=0$$
along every curve $\gamma_p$; here $D_\lambda$ is the covariant derivative along a curve from [[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]. For each $p\in U$, let $J_{\mathrm{reg}}(p)$ be the connected component containing $0$ of the parameter values for which $d(F_\lambda)_p:T_pU\to T_{F(p,\lambda)}M$ is injective and the pullback form $(X,Y)\mapsto g(d(F_\lambda)_pX,d(F_\lambda)_pY)$ is positive definite on $T_pU$. Require, for every $\lambda\in J$, that its variation directions satisfy
$$g_{F(p,\lambda)}\bigl(\ell(p,\lambda),dF_{(p,\lambda)}(X,0)\bigr)=0\qquad(X\in T_pU).$$
Thus its variation directions are orthogonal to $\ell$. For $\lambda\in J_{\mathrm{reg}}(p)$, the map $F$ has rank three locally near $(p,\lambda)$: its two section directions are spacelike and orthogonal to the nonzero null vector $\ell$. Its local image is a null hypersurface, with tangent space $\ell^\perp$ and induced radical $\mathbb R\ell$, as in [[lem-gr-fx-null-normal-plane-and-screen]]. The parameter $\lambda$ is affine. On each section in $J_{\mathrm{reg}}$, the **screen** is $\mathscr S=\ell^\perp/\mathbb R\ell$ with metric $\bar q([X],[Y])=g(X,Y)$; it is the positive two-dimensional quotient, identified isometrically with the tangent plane of that section by projection. The induced form on the full null hypersurface has radical $\mathbb R\ell$ and has no inverse. All traces and inverses in this definition are taken on the screen.

All screen bundles associated with this congruence are understood as bundles over the parameter domain $U\times J$: the notation $\mathscr S_{F(p,\lambda)}$ denotes the branch determined by $(p,\lambda)$, so self-intersections do not identify distinct screen fibers. For each $\lambda\in J$, the screen Jacobi map $A_\lambda:T_pS\to\mathscr S_{F(p,\lambda)}$ sends $X$ to the screen class of the variation field $J_X(\lambda):=dF_{(p,\lambda)}(X,0)$; it is invertible for $\lambda\in J_{\mathrm{reg}}(p)$. A **focal instant** is a positive parameter in $J$ where $A_\lambda$ loses rank; the **first focal instant**, if it exists, is the least such parameter after $0$. Along an affine generator the screen derivative is $\mathcal D_\ell[X]:=[D_\ell X]$; it is independent of the representative, by the preceding lemma. On $J_{\mathrm{reg}}$, the derivative $A_\lambda'$ is taken using $\mathcal D_\ell$, and the **optical endomorphism** is $B_\lambda:=A_\lambda'A_\lambda^{-1}$. Its **optical expansion** is $\theta:=\operatorname{tr}B$, and its **optical shear** is $\sigma:=B-\frac12\theta\,\mathrm{id}_{\mathscr S}$. Since the congruence is normal to a null hypersurface, $B$ is self-adjoint. Its antisymmetric part $\omega:=(B-B^*)/2$, called the twist, therefore vanishes. At $\lambda=0$, $B$ is the endomorphism $q^{-1}\chi_\ell$ and these optical quantities agree with $\theta_\ell,\sigma_\ell$.

No orientation of $M$, $S$, or the screen is required for these constructions. Indeed, if two orthonormal screen frames are related by a real $2\times2$ matrix $O$ with $O^{\mathsf T}O=I_2$, then the endomorphism matrices obey $\widehat B=O^{-1}BO$ and $\widehat\sigma=O^{-1}\sigma O$. Cyclicity of the matrix trace gives $\operatorname{tr}\widehat B=\operatorname{tr}B$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\widehat\sigma^2)=\operatorname{tr}(\sigma^2)=|\sigma|_{\bar q}^2$; the last equality follows by summing the squared entries of the symmetric shear matrix in an orthonormal frame. This includes $\det O=-1$. The screen inner products and the rank of $A_\lambda$ are likewise invariant under changes of frame, so neither the index-form contractions nor the focal condition uses a signed screen area form. The preceding lemma constructs normal pairs using the supplied time orientation and only a local spacelike complement; changing the complement's sign interchanges the two future null rays. No global ordered pair follows. If an orientation is additionally supplied, the same formulas apply on that oriented subclass.

causal-curve and push-up results. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold. Let $S$ be a smooth embedded two-manifold without
boundary whose induced metric $q:=g|_{TS}$ is positive definite, and let
$p\in S$. Choose an open neighborhood $U\subseteq S$ of $p$ and a smooth
future null normal field $\ell$ along $U$, so
$g(\ell_q,Y)=0$ for every $q\in U$ and $Y\in T_qS$.
Let $\gamma:[0,L_1]\to M$ be smooth up to its endpoints, with
$$\gamma(0)=p,\qquad \dot\gamma(0)=\ell_p,\qquad g(\dot\gamma,\dot\gamma)=0,\qquad g(\dot\gamma,N)<0,\qquad D_\lambda\dot\gamma=0.$$
Here $D_\lambda$ is covariant differentiation along the curve. Put
$\chi_\ell(X,Y):=g(\nabla_X\ell,Y)$ as in
[[def-gr-fx-null-screen-geometry]], and set $B_0:T_pS\to T_pS$ by
$q(B_0X,Y)=\chi_\ell(X,Y)$ for all $X,Y\in T_pS$.
The screen along $\gamma$ is
$$\mathscr S_\lambda:=\dot\gamma(\lambda)^\perp/\mathbb R\dot\gamma(\lambda),$$
with its positive metric and screen derivative $\mathcal D_\lambda$ from
[[def-gr-fx-null-screen-geometry]]. Define
$$\mathcal R_\lambda[X]:=[R(X,\dot\gamma)\dot\gamma].$$
A **normal screen Jacobi field** is a smooth section $J$ of $\mathscr S$ that
satisfies $\mathcal D_\lambda^2J+\mathcal R_\lambda J=0$ and the initial
conditions $J(0)=[X]$, $\mathcal D_\lambda J(0)=B_0X$ for some
$X\in T_pS$. A **focal instant** $\lambda_0\in(0,L_1]$ is a parameter at
which such a field with $X\ne0$ has $J(\lambda_0)=0$.

Put $I^+(S):=\bigcup_{p\in S}I^+(p)$,
$J^+(S):=\bigcup_{p\in S}J^+(p)$, and
$E^+(S):=J^+(S)\setminus I^+(S)$, using the causal-reachability conventions
of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]].

If $\lambda_0$ is a focal instant, there is $\varepsilon>0$ such that
$$\gamma(\lambda)\in I^+(S)\qquad (\lambda_0<\lambda<\lambda_0+\varepsilon).$$
Consequently, no point on this portion of the generator belongs to
$E^+(S)$. The conclusion is local along the generator and does not assert
geodesic incompleteness or curvature blow-up. In an SI interpretation take
$x^0=ct$ and $\lambda$ in metres; the proof itself is independent of units.

derivations.claim:
Since $e^f>0$, the boost preserves the future null rays, and
$g(\ell',k')=e^fe^{-f}g(\ell,k)=-2$. The boost law in [F1] gives
$\widehat\theta_0=e^f\theta_0$, so $\widehat\theta_0$ has the same sign as $\theta_0$.
The new tangent is $\ell'=d/d\lambda'$, while $\ell=d/d\lambda$; solving
$d\lambda/d\lambda'=e^f$ with both parameters zero at the initial section
gives $\lambda'=e^{-f}\lambda$ because $f$ is constant along the generator.

Since $d/d\lambda'=e^f d/d\lambda$, [F1] gives
$\widehat B=e^fB$, $\widehat\sigma=e^f\sigma$, and
$\widehat\theta=e^f\theta$. Therefore
$d\widehat\theta/d\lambda'=e^{2f}d\theta/d\lambda$ and
$|\widehat\sigma|^2=e^{2f}|\sigma|^2$. Tensoriality gives
$\operatorname{Ric}(\ell',\ell')=e^{2f}\operatorname{Ric}(\ell,\ell)$.
Multiplying the Raychaudhuri equation in [F2] by $e^{2f}$ proves its form is
unchanged. If $\theta_0<0$, then
$$\lambda'_* =\frac2{|\widehat\theta_0|} =e^{-f}\frac2{|\theta_0|}=e^{-f}\lambda_*.$$

The screen Jacobi map is reparametrized by
$\widehat A_{\lambda'}=A_{e^f\lambda'}$, so its rank-loss event is the same point
of $M$ and its parameter value is multiplied by $e^{-f}$. By [F3], the
geometric statement that points just beyond that event lie in $I^+(S)$ is
unchanged by relabeling the affine parameter. Thus only the numerical affine
label changes; the causal-boundary conclusion does not.

two-surface. Put $I^+(S):=\bigcup_{p\in S}I^+(p)$,
$J^+(S):=\bigcup_{p\in S}J^+(p)$, and
$E^+(S):=J^+(S)\setminus I^+(S)$, using the causal-reachability conventions
of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. Let
$\gamma:[0,L_1]\to M$ be a future affinely parametrized null geodesic
orthogonal to $S$ at $p=\gamma(0)$, with initial tangent $\ell$ and null
second fundamental form $\chi_\ell$ as in
[[def-gr-fx-null-screen-geometry]]. A **focal instant** $\lambda_0>0$ is an
instant at which a nonzero screen Jacobi field arising from variation of the
initial point in $S$, with initial screen derivative determined by
$q^{-1}\chi_\ell$, has zero screen value.

If $\lambda_0$ is a focal instant, there is $\varepsilon>0$ such that
$$\gamma(\lambda)\in I^+(S)\qquad (\lambda_0<\lambda<\lambda_0+\varepsilon).$$
Consequently, no point on this portion of the generator belongs to
$E^+(S)$. The conclusion is local along the generator and does not assert
geodesic incompleteness or curvature blow-up. In an SI interpretation take
$x^0=ct$ and $\lambda$ in metres; the proof itself is independent of units.

citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary, so that $M$ is Hausdorff
and second countable and carries a maximal smooth atlas
([[def-smooth-manifold]]). Let $g$ be a smooth covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$
in the sense of [[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]. Then $g$ assigns
to every $p\in M$ a bilinear form $g_p:T_pM\times T_pM\to\mathbb R$
([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]).

**(a) Lorentzian metric.** The field $g$ is a **Lorentzian metric of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$** on $M$ when it is symmetric and nondegenerate, and at every
$p\in M$ the pair $(T_pM,g_p)$ is a Lorentz vector space of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ in the sense of [[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]: that is, $g_p$ has
inertia $(3,1,0)$, so that some — equivalently every — basis of $T_pM$ in which
the matrix of $g_p$ is diagonal has exactly one negative and three positive
diagonal entries. The pair $(M,g)$ is a **smooth Lorentzian four-manifold** (or
Lorentzian manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$). In a smooth chart $(U,x)$ the
**components** of $g$ are the $C^\infty$ functions
$g_{ab}(q)=g_q(\partial_a|_q,\partial_b|_q)$ of
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]], and $g_{ab}=g_{ba}$ by symmetry.
We use indices $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$ and the Einstein summation convention, with
components in a chart written as lower-case indexed symbols and equations
between indexed fields understood basis-independently. These conventions are
fixed once for this library and the physical reading of the symbols is recorded
with the framework postulates, separately from this mathematical definition.

**(b) Pointwise causal structure.** For every $p\in M$ the vocabulary of
[[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] applies to the Lorentz vector
space $(T_pM,g_p)$: a tangent vector $v\in T_pM$ is **timelike** when
$g_p(v,v)<0$, **null** when $v\neq0$ and $g_p(v,v)=0$, **spacelike** when
$g_p(v,v)>0$, and **causal** when it is timelike or null. Every nonzero
$v\in T_pM$ has exactly one causal character. The **timelike set**
$T_p:=\{v\in T_pM:g_p(v,v)<0\}$ has exactly two connected components, each
nonempty, open, convex and path-connected; each $g_p$-orthonormal basis
$e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3$ of $T_pM$ satisfies $g_p(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$
for some ordering, so in particular nonzero orthonormal vectors exist at every
point ([[lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis]],
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]]).

**(c) Time orientation.** A **time orientation** of $(M,g)$, also called a
**choice of future cone**, is a smooth vector field $N$ on $M$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]], whose tangent-bundle
smooth structure uses the axiom $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of
[[def-countable-choice]]; this is the only use of that axiom in this
definition) such that

$$g_p(N_p,N_p)<0\qquad\text{for every }p\in M .$$

The function $p\mapsto g_p(N_p,N_p)$ is $C^\infty$ because $g$ is a smooth
covariant $2$-tensor field and $N$ a smooth field, so the condition is a
pointwise strict inequality between a smooth function and $0$; since
$g_p(N_p,N_p)<0$ implies $N_p\neq0$, a time orientation is nowhere vanishing.
A **time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold** is a triple $(M,g,N)$
consisting of a smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and a time orientation $N$.

Given a time orientation $N$ and $p\in M$, the vector $N_p$ is timelike, and we
**define** a nonzero causal vector $v\in T_pM$ to be **future-directed** when
$g_p(v,N_p)<0$ and **past-directed** when $g_p(v,N_p)>0$. The classification of
nonzero causal vectors into exactly these two classes, and its agreement with
the two components of the timelike set (the future component is the component
$C_p^+$ containing $N_p$, and the future causal vectors form
$\operatorname{cl}(C_p^+)\setminus\{0\}$), is proved in
[[lem-gr-future-causal-classification-by-a-timelike-field]]; in particular no
nonzero causal $v$ satisfies $g_p(v,N_p)=0$, so the definition is exhaustive and
mutually exclusive. Replacing $N$ by $-N$ reverses every future/past label, and
two time orientations $N,N'$ determine the same future-directed causal vectors
at every point where $g_p(N_p,N'_p)<0$, while they determine opposite ones
where $g_p(N_p,N'_p)>0$, by
[[lem-gr-timelike-fields-define-equal-or-opposite-future-cones]]; that lemma
also shows the sign of $p\mapsto g_p(N_p,N'_p)$ is constant on every connected
component of $M$.

**(d) The inverse metric.** Because $g_p$ is nondegenerate, it induces at each
$p$ an isomorphism $\flat_p:T_pM\to T_p^*M$, $v\mapsto g_p(v,\cdot)$, and an
inverse metric $g_p^{-1}$ on the dual space; the inverse metric, the musical
isomorphisms and the components $g^{ab}$ are defined separately on this page,
where the smoothness of those components is also proved. Neither construction
uses any choice principle beyond the one already recorded in (c).


**(e) Smooth timelike curves and their scalar normalization.** Before using
these quantities in the physical conventions, fix a positive real scaling
parameter $c$ (with no physical meaning or dimension in this mathematical
item). A **smooth future timelike curve** is a smooth map $\gamma:I\to M$
from a nonempty open real interval $I$ ([[def-interval]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]) whose velocity derivation
$\gamma'(s)\in T_{\gamma(s)}M$
([[def-velocity-derivation-of-a-smooth-curve]]) satisfies
$g(\gamma',\gamma')<0$ and $g(\gamma',N)<0$ at every $s\in I$.
In a chart its components are $d(x^a\circ\gamma)/ds$, $a=0,1,2,3$.
For a supplied base point $s_0\in I$ and additive constant $\tau_0\in\mathbb R$
define

$$h(s):=\sqrt{-g_{\gamma(s)}(\gamma'(s),\gamma'(s))},\qquad \tau(s):=\tau_0+\frac1c\int_{s_0}^{s}h(r)\,dr,\qquad U(s):=\frac{c\gamma'(s)}{h(s)}.$$

The integral is oriented when $s<s_0$. The function $\tau$ is called
**proper time** for this scaling and $U$ the **four-velocity** of the smooth
curve; its increment times $c$ is the Lorentzian length. The well-definedness
proof below shows $\tau'>0$, that $\tau:I\to\tau(I)$ is a smooth
diffeomorphism, and that $U$ is the velocity of $\gamma\circ\tau^{-1}$.
Thus $g(U,U)=-c^2$ and $U$ is future timelike. This introduces the smooth
case before any physical unit reading; the later worldline definition extends
it to its stated $C^k$, endpoint and piecewise-$C^1$ classes. It asserts no
clock coupling, motion law or physical value of $c$.

**Convention and scope.** The physical reading of a smooth time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold as a classical spacetime model, and the domain in which
that reading is adopted, are recorded in the framework postulate
`post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain`; the words spacetime and event carry no
mathematical content beyond this definition, and this item asserts no claim
about nature. The dimension $4$ and the absence of boundary are part of the
data; nothing in the definition assumes that $M$ is nonempty or connected, and
no completeness, extendibility or maximality property of $(M,g)$ is asserted.

A **smooth $n$-manifold** is a pair $(M,\mathcal S)$ in which $M$ is a
topological $n$-manifold
([[def-topological-manifold-without-boundary]]) and $\mathcal S$ is a **smooth
structure** on $M$: a maximal smooth atlas
([[thm-each-smooth-atlas-is-contained-in-a-unique-maximal-smooth-atlas]]).
Because
[[thm-each-smooth-atlas-is-contained-in-a-unique-maximal-smooth-atlas]] sends
every smooth atlas to the unique maximal atlas containing it, a smooth manifold
is equivalently specified by a topological manifold $M$ together with any one
smooth atlas $\mathcal A$, the structure being the generated $[\mathcal A]$. A
chart $(U,\varphi)\in\mathcal S$ is called a **smooth chart** (or a **chart of
the smooth structure**); its domain is a **coordinate domain** and its
coordinate functions are **smooth coordinates** on $U$. When the structure is
clear from context, the manifold itself is written $M$ in place of
$(M,\mathcal S)$.

Let $M$ be a smooth manifold. A **smooth tensor field of type $(r,s)$** on $M$
is a smooth section of the tensor bundle $T^r_sM\to M$.

A **Riemannian metric** on a Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold $M$ is a smooth symmetric covariant two-tensor $g$ such that $g_p(v,v)>0$ for every point $p$ and every nonzero $v\in T_pM$. A **Riemannian manifold** is the pair $(M,g)$.

This is a [[def-smooth-tensor-field]] giving a [[def-smooth-bundle-metric]] on $TM$. Dimension zero is allowed: its zero bilinear form is positive definite because there are no nonzero vectors. The empty manifold has its unique empty metric. Boundaries are allowed where stated, with smoothness understood up to the boundary.
Every supplied smooth Riemannian metric on a smooth manifold, including a manifold with boundary, has exactly one Levi–Civita connection. The construction adds no choice assumption.

Let $a \in \mathbb{R}$, where $\mathbb{R}$ is the ambient ordered field
(Ordered field, Field).

**Natural exponents.** By the recursion theorem (The recursion theorem) applied to
the set $\mathbb{R}$, the starting element $1$ and the function
$f(x) = x \cdot a$, there is a unique function $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$,
written $n \mapsto a^n$, with

$$a^0 = 1, \qquad a^{n+1} = a^n \cdot a \quad (n \in \mathbb{N}).$$

Thus $a^1 = a$, $a^2 = a \cdot a$, and so on. Note that this is defined for
**every** $a$, including $a = 0$.

**Negative exponents.** If $a \ne 0$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$ with $n \ge 1$, set

$$a^{-n} := (a^n)^{-1}.$$

**Why that is legitimate.** The right-hand side presupposes that $a^n$ is
invertible, that is, that $a^n \ne 0$. This is a proof obligation and not an
observation, and it is discharged by claim 2 of Laws of integer exponents: for $a \ne 0$
in a field, $a^n \ne 0$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, proved there by induction on
$n$ from the fact that a field has no zero divisors (A field has no zero divisors: $ab = 0 \Rightarrow a = 0$ or $b = 0$).
That lemma is a statement *about* the operation introduced here, so it depends on
this definition and is recorded in this item's `justified_by` rather than in its
`deps` (SCHEMA §3). Given $a^n \ne 0$, the value $(a^n)^{-1}$ is a single
well-determined element, because multiplicative inverses in a field are unique
(Identities and inverses in a field are unique).

**Integer exponents.** Every integer $m$ (The integers as equivalence classes of pairs of naturals) is either
$n$ or $-n$ for a unique natural $n$, where $n$ in these integer expressions denotes its image under the
embedding $\iota : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}$ (The naturals embed in the integers,
Arithmetic on the integers). This too is a citation and not a slogan: the order on
$\mathbb{Z}$ is total (The integers form a totally ordered ring), so $m \ge 0$ or $m < 0$; the
image of $\iota$ is exactly the set of nonnegative integers, and each of them is
$n$ for a unique natural $n$ (The naturals embed in the integers); and if $m < 0$ then
$-m > 0$, by compatibility of the order with addition (The integers form a totally ordered ring),
so $-m = n$ and $m = -n$, with $n$ unique because $\iota$ is
injective. The two clauses above therefore define $a^m$ for every
$m \in \mathbb{Z}$ whenever $a \ne 0$, and for every $m \in \mathbb{N}$ for
arbitrary $a$. The two exponent domains are disjoint: the natural clause
handles $m \ge 0$, including $m = 0$, while the negative clause requires
$n \ge 1$ and therefore handles only $m < 0$.

Let $a, b$ be elements of a field ([[def-field]]) and let integer powers be as in
[[def-integer-power]].

1. For all $m, n \in \mathbb{N}$: $a^{m+n} = a^m a^n$, $(a^m)^n = a^{mn}$ and $(ab)^n = a^n b^n$.
2. If $a \ne 0$ then $a^n \ne 0$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, and $a^{-m} = (a^m)^{-1}$ for every $m \in \mathbb{Z}$ ([[def-int-operations]]).
3. If $a \ne 0$ and $b \ne 0$ then all three identities of claim 1 hold for all $m, n \in \mathbb{Z}$.

Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, let $c \in A$ be a limit point of $A$
(Limit point, isolated point, adherent point, derived set, and dense subset of $\mathbb{R}$), let $f, g : A \to \mathbb{R}$ be differentiable at $c$
(The derivative $f'(c) = \lim_{x \to c} \frac{f(x) - f(c)}{x - c}$ of $f : A \to \mathbb{R}$ at a point $c \in A$ that is a limit point of $A$, and differentiability on a set) and let $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$. Then:

1. $f + g$ is differentiable at $c$ and $(f+g)'(c) = f'(c) + g'(c)$;
2. $\alpha f$ is differentiable at $c$ and $(\alpha f)'(c) = \alpha f'(c)$;
3. $fg$ is differentiable at $c$ and $(fg)'(c) = f'(c)g(c) + f(c)g'(c)$;
4. if $g(c) \ne 0$ then, writing $A_0 := \{\, x \in A : g(x) \ne 0 \,\}$, the
   point $c$ lies in $A_0$ and is a limit point of $A_0$, the quotient
   $(f/g)|_{A_0} : A_0 \to \mathbb{R}$, $x \mapsto f(x)/g(x)$, is differentiable
   at $c$ as a function on $A_0$, and
   $$\bigl((f/g)|_{A_0}\bigr)'(c) \;=\; \frac{f'(c)\,g(c) - f(c)\,g'(c)}{g(c)^{2}} .$$

Each claim asserts two things: that the derivative on the left exists, and that
it has the stated value. Both are proved.

**Why claim 4 is stated on $A_0$.** The function $f/g$ is not defined where $g$
vanishes, and $g$ may vanish at points of $A$ far from $c$; restricting to $A_0$
is forced. That the restriction still has $c$ as a limit point, so that a
derivative there means anything at all, is not free either, and it is the last
claim of If $\lim_{x \to c} f(x) = L \ne 0$ then $|f| > |L|/2$ on a punctured neighbourhood of $c$; in particular if $L > 0$ then $f > L/2 > 0$ there applied to $g$. The hypothesis
is $g(c) \ne 0$, not "$g$ vanishes nowhere".

**Everything is proved through
Carathéodory's characterisation: $f$ is differentiable at $c$ if and only if there is $\varphi : A \to \mathbb{R}$, continuous at $c$, with $f(x) - f(c) = \varphi(x)(x - c)$ for every $x \in A$, and then $\varphi$ is unique and $\varphi(c) = f'(c)$.** No difference quotient is estimated and
no limit theorem beyond continuity is used, so no choice principle is spent.
The four identities are four algebraic rearrangements of an increment, each
followed by a reading of Sums, scalar multiples, products, absolute values, maxima, minima and quotients with nonvanishing denominator of continuous functions are continuous, as are constants, the identity and every polynomial function.

Let $k\in\mathbb N$. Finite componentwise sums and products of $C^k$ Euclidean maps are $C^k$, and a composite of composable $C^k$ Euclidean maps is $C^k$. Scalar multiples are included among the finite componentwise operations. The assertions remain valid on an empty open domain.

Let $M$, $N$, $P$ be smooth manifolds.

1. The identity map $\mathrm{id}_M:M\to M$ is smooth.
2. If $F:M\to N$ and $G:N\to P$ are smooth, then $G\circ F:M\to P$ is smooth.

In coordinates for a Riemannian metric with matrix $(g_{ij})$ and inverse $(g^{ij})$, its Levi–Civita symbols are
$$\Gamma^k{}_{ij}=\tfrac12\sum_\ell g^{k\ell}(\partial_i g_{j\ell}+\partial_j g_{i\ell}-\partial_\ell g_{ij}).$$

Let $\nabla$ be an affine connection on a smooth manifold $M$. For $p\in M$
and $u,v,w\in T_pM$, choose smooth local extensions $X,Y,Z$ and set

$$R_p(u,v)w:=(R(X,Y)Z)_p.$$

This is independent of the extensions, is trilinear in $(u,v,w)$, and varies
smoothly with $p$. Equivalently,

$$\mathcal R_p(\alpha,u,v,w):=\alpha\bigl(R_p(u,v)w\bigr)$$

is a smooth type $(1,3)$ tensor field. We use $R$ for both this tensor and its
vector-valued representative.

Let $T$ be a type $(r,s)$ tensor on $V$ with $r,s\ge 1$. Contracting the first
contravariant slot against the first covariant slot gives the type
$(r-1,s-1)$ tensor $\operatorname{ctr}(T)$ defined intrinsically by

$$ \operatorname{ctr}(T)(\alpha_2,\ldots,\alpha_r,v_2,\ldots,v_s) :=\sum_i T(e^i,\alpha_2,\ldots,\alpha_r,e_i,v_2,\ldots,v_s), $$

where $(e_i)$ is any basis of $V$ and $(e^i)$ its dual basis. The next lemma
shows that this formula is basis-independent.

The contraction formula

$$ \sum_i T(e^i,\alpha_2,\ldots,\alpha_r,e_i,v_2,\ldots,v_s) $$

has the same value for every basis $(e_i)$ and its dual basis $(e^i)$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$ and Einstein tensor $G$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]), let
$\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a spacelike embedded hypersurface
([[def-embedded-submanifold-and-slice-chart]],
[[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (a)), and fix real
constants $\kappa$ and $\Lambda$ (the framework coupling constants, purely
parameters for this definition).

**(a) The geometric data.**
For $p\in\Sigma$ the orthogonal complement $T_p\Sigma^{\perp}$ is
one-dimensional and nondegenerate
([[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]],
[[lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis]]); there is therefore a unique
$n_p\in T_p\Sigma^{\perp}$ with $g_p(n_p,n_p)=-1$ and $g_p(n_p,N_p)<0$ and it
depends smoothly on $p$, the **future unit normal field** of $\Sigma$; this
and the properties of $h$ and $K$ below are proved, not assumed, in
[[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]. Define
on $\Sigma$ the **induced metric** $h$ and the **second fundamental form**
$K$ by
$$h_p(V,W):=g_p(V,W),\qquad K_p(V,W):=g_p(\nabla_Vn,W)\qquad(V,W\in T_p\Sigma),$$
where $\nabla_Vn$ is the covariant derivative at $p$ of the ambient field $n$
in the tangential direction $V$; $h$ is a smooth Riemannian metric on
$\Sigma$ and $K$ a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $\Sigma$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]).

**(b) Matter data and constraints.** Let $T$ be a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field on $M$ (the stress-energy field of a matter branch). Its
**matter data on $\Sigma$** are the smooth fields
$$\rho:=T(n,n),\qquad j(V):=-T(n,V)\quad(V\in T\Sigma).$$
The tuple $(\Sigma,h,K,\rho,j)$ **satisfies the constraint equations** for
$(\kappa,\Lambda)$ when
$$G(n,n)-\Lambda=\kappa\,\rho,\qquad G(n,V)=\kappa\,T(n,V)\quad\text{for every }V\in T_p\Sigma,\ p\in\Sigma .$$
The first is the normal projection of the equation $G+\Lambda g=\kappa T$
evaluated on $(n,n)$, namely $G(n,n)+\Lambda g(n,n)=\kappa T(n,n)$, with
$g(n,n)=-1$; the second is the normal-tangential projection, the term in
$\Lambda$ dropping because $g(n,V)=0$. That a solution of the field equation
satisfies these two projections is proved in
[[lem-gr-constraint-projections]]. The purely tangential projection
$G(V,W)+\Lambda h(V,W)=\kappa T(V,W)$ is not part of the constraints and is
not required here.

**(c) Developments.** A **development** of the data
$(\Sigma,h,K,\rho,j)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
$(M',g',N')$ together with a smooth embedding $\varphi:\Sigma\to M'$ whose
image is a spacelike embedded hypersurface with induced metric $\varphi^*g'=h$
and second fundamental form $K$ with respect to its future unit normal $n'$.
Write $T'$ for the smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field included as
the development's stress-energy field. Require the tensor equation
$$G'+\Lambda g'=\kappa T'$$
at every point of $M'$, where $G'$ is the Einstein tensor of $g'$ with its
metric-selected connection, defined as above. The constants $\kappa$ and
$\Lambda$ are the fixed parameters of the initial data. The matter-data matching condition is
the pair of normal projections
$$\rho(p)=T'_{\varphi(p)}(n'_{\varphi(p)},n'_{\varphi(p)}),\qquad j_p(V)=-T'_{\varphi(p)}(n'_{\varphi(p)},d\varphi_p(V))\quad(p\in\Sigma,\ V\in T_p\Sigma).$$
Equivalently, the scalar field $T'(n',n')$ along $\varphi(\Sigma)$ pulls
back to $\rho$, and the covector field $-T'(n',\cdot)$ restricted to
$T\varphi(\Sigma)$ pulls back to $j$. This tuple prescribes only these
stress-energy projections; any additional matter-field data are not included
in $(\Sigma,h,K,\rho,j)$. The development is a **globally hyperbolic
development** when
$\varphi(\Sigma)$ is a Cauchy hypersurface of $(M',g',N')$. The implication
from this Cauchy property to global hyperbolicity of $(M',g',N')$ is a
separate theorem, deferred to the later causal theory; it is not established
by this definition
([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]],
[[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (c)).

**(d) Maximality.** A globally hyperbolic development $(M_*,g_*,N_*;
\varphi_*)$ is **maximal** for the data when for every globally hyperbolic
development $(M',g',N';\varphi')$ there is a smooth isometric embedding
$\psi:M'\to M_*$ with $\psi\circ\varphi'=\varphi_*$, $\psi$ preserving the
time orientations and carrying the selected stress-energy tensor $T'$ to
$T_*$, that is, $\psi^*T_*=T'$. This is a universal embedding property: every globally hyperbolic
development embeds into the selected maximal one with its data and
stress-energy tensor preserved. It does not assert that arbitrary globally
hyperbolic developments are mutually isometric.

**(e) Scope.** The definition asserts neither existence nor uniqueness of
developments, and it does not assert that $T'$ is generated by matter fields
solving any equation: those claims require the local and global existence theory of
the Einstein-matter system and are not made on this page. The constraint
equations are displayed only as equations satisfied or not by given data.
The equivalent formulation of the constraints in terms of the induced scalar
curvature of $h$ and the divergence of $K$, and the existence theory for
solutions of the constraints, rest on the Gauss-Codazzi relations and on PDE
theory and are deferred to the later pages of this track; no such
equivalence is asserted here.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, and let $\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a smooth spacelike embedded hypersurface with future unit normal $n$, induced Riemannian metric $h$ and second fundamental form $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_Xn,Y)$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]], [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]). Write $D$ for the Levi-Civita connection of $h$, $R^h$ for its curvature operator in the same operator convention as the ambient curvature, and $S_h$ for its scalar curvature. Explicitly distinguish the lowered tensor from the operator pairing by setting
$$\mathcal R^g(A,B,C,D):=g(R^g(C,D)B,A),\qquad \mathcal R^h(A,B,C,D):=h(R^h(C,D)B,A).$$
Thus $\mathcal R^g_{abcd}=R_{abcd}$ in [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]; in particular $g(R^g(X,Y)Z,W)=\mathcal R^g(W,Z,X,Y)$. Let $G$ be the Einstein tensor defined there. At every $p\in\Sigma$ and for all $X,Y,Z,W\in T_p\Sigma$:

**(a) Gauss equation.**
$$\mathcal R^g(X,Y,Z,W)=\mathcal R^h(X,Y,Z,W)+K(X,Z)K(Y,W)-K(X,W)K(Y,Z).$$
Equivalently, in operator order,
$$g(R^g(X,Y)Z,W)=h(R^h(X,Y)Z,W)+K(Y,Z)K(X,W)-K(X,Z)K(Y,W).$$

**(b) Codazzi equation.**
$$g(R^g(X,Y)Z,n)=(D_YK)(X,Z)-(D_XK)(Y,Z).$$

**(c) Normal projections.** Define $(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)=h^{ij}(D_{e_i}K)(e_j,Y)$, $\tau=\operatorname{tr}_hK=h^{ij}K_{ij}$ and $|K|_h^2=h^{ik}h^{jl}K_{ij}K_{kl}$. Then
$$G(n,n)=\tfrac12(S_h+\tau^2-|K|_h^2),\qquad G(n,Y)=(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau.$$

**(d) Constraint equations.** If the tensor equation $G+\Lambda g=\kappa T$ holds at $p$, for a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor $T$ and real constants $\kappa,\Lambda$, then
$$S_h+\tau^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T(n,n),\qquad (\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau=\kappa T(n,Y).$$
With $\rho=T(n,n)$ and $j(Y)=-T(n,Y)$, the second equation is $(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau=-\kappa j(Y)$.

derivations.claim:
For each integer $n\ge1$, induction by the product rule gives
$(t^n)'=nt^{n-1}$, and the quotient rule on $t>0$ gives
$(t^{-n})'=-nt^{-n-1}$; iterating this identity shows that every derivative
of $t\mapsto t^{-2}$ is a constant multiple of a negative integer power, hence
is continuous on $(0,\infty)$. The map $t\mapsto t^4$ is a polynomial.
Thus both maps are smooth there; [F5] gives their $C^k$ regularity at every
finite order and [F6] makes their composites with $\phi$ smooth. Hence
$h=\phi^4\widetilde h$ is smooth,
symmetric and positive definite, because for every nonzero $v\in T_p\Sigma$,
$h_p(v,v)=\phi(p)^4\widetilde h_p(v,v)>0$ by [F2]. The same rules show that
$K=\phi^{-2}\widetilde\sigma+(\tau/3)h$ is smooth and symmetric. The
Riemannian connection theorem [F3] supplies both $\widetilde D$ and $D$.

In each chart $\det(\widetilde h_{ij})>0$ and
$\widetilde h^{ij}=\operatorname{adj}(\widetilde h)_{ij}/\det(\widetilde h)$;
the adjugate entries are polynomials in the smooth metric components [F1],
and the reciprocal is smooth by the same quotient-rule induction as in the
earlier proof step 1.1 and finite-order algebra closure [F5]. Thus
$\widetilde h^{ij}$ is smooth;
$h^{ij}=\phi^{-4}\widetilde h^{ij}$ is smooth by step 1.1. Formula [F7]
therefore makes the Christoffel symbols smooth, so the displayed Laplacian is
defined for smooth $f$. By [F8] curvature is tensorial, and by [F9, F10] its
Ricci and scalar contractions do not depend on the chart. The same
basis-independent contractions define the traces and squared norms; all
derivative terms use the connections supplied by [F3].

For data induced by an embedded spacelike hypersurface, the convention in
[F11] fixes the sign of $K$, and [F12] gives precisely the stated Hamiltonian
and momentum residuals when $\Lambda=0$ and stress-energy vanishes. The
abstract data definition itself makes no embedding or development assertion.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary, so that $M$ is Hausdorff
and second countable and carries a maximal smooth atlas
([[def-smooth-manifold]]). Let $g$ be a smooth covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$
in the sense of [[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]. Then $g$ assigns
to every $p\in M$ a bilinear form $g_p:T_pM\times T_pM\to\mathbb R$
([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]).

**(a) Lorentzian metric.** The field $g$ is a **Lorentzian metric of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$** on $M$ when it is symmetric and nondegenerate, and at every
$p\in M$ the pair $(T_pM,g_p)$ is a Lorentz vector space of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ in the sense of [[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]: that is, $g_p$ has
inertia $(3,1,0)$, so that some — equivalently every — basis of $T_pM$ in which
the matrix of $g_p$ is diagonal has exactly one negative and three positive
diagonal entries. The pair $(M,g)$ is a **smooth Lorentzian four-manifold** (or
Lorentzian manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$). In a smooth chart $(U,x)$ the
**components** of $g$ are the $C^\infty$ functions
$g_{ab}(q)=g_q(\partial_a|_q,\partial_b|_q)$ of
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]], and $g_{ab}=g_{ba}$ by symmetry.
We use indices $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$ and the Einstein summation convention, with
components in a chart written as lower-case indexed symbols and equations
between indexed fields understood basis-independently. These conventions are
fixed once for this library and the physical reading of the symbols is recorded
with the framework postulates, separately from this mathematical definition.

**(b) Pointwise causal structure.** For every $p\in M$ the vocabulary of
[[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] applies to the Lorentz vector
space $(T_pM,g_p)$: a tangent vector $v\in T_pM$ is **timelike** when
$g_p(v,v)<0$, **null** when $v\neq0$ and $g_p(v,v)=0$, **spacelike** when
$g_p(v,v)>0$, and **causal** when it is timelike or null. Every nonzero
$v\in T_pM$ has exactly one causal character. The **timelike set**
$T_p:=\{v\in T_pM:g_p(v,v)<0\}$ has exactly two connected components, each
nonempty, open, convex and path-connected; each $g_p$-orthonormal basis
$e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3$ of $T_pM$ satisfies $g_p(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$
for some ordering, so in particular nonzero orthonormal vectors exist at every
point ([[lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis]],
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]]).

**(c) Time orientation.** A **time orientation** of $(M,g)$, also called a
**choice of future cone**, is a smooth vector field $N$ on $M$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]], whose tangent-bundle
smooth structure uses the axiom $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of
[[def-countable-choice]]; this is the only use of that axiom in this
definition) such that

$$g_p(N_p,N_p)<0\qquad\text{for every }p\in M .$$

The function $p\mapsto g_p(N_p,N_p)$ is $C^\infty$ because $g$ is a smooth
covariant $2$-tensor field and $N$ a smooth field, so the condition is a
pointwise strict inequality between a smooth function and $0$; since
$g_p(N_p,N_p)<0$ implies $N_p\neq0$, a time orientation is nowhere vanishing.
A **time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold** is a triple $(M,g,N)$
consisting of a smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and a time orientation $N$.

Given a time orientation $N$ and $p\in M$, the vector $N_p$ is timelike, and we
**define** a nonzero causal vector $v\in T_pM$ to be **future-directed** when
$g_p(v,N_p)<0$ and **past-directed** when $g_p(v,N_p)>0$. The classification of
nonzero causal vectors into exactly these two classes, and its agreement with
the two components of the timelike set (the future component is the component
$C_p^+$ containing $N_p$, and the future causal vectors form
$\operatorname{cl}(C_p^+)\setminus\{0\}$), is proved in
[[lem-gr-future-causal-classification-by-a-timelike-field]]; in particular no
nonzero causal $v$ satisfies $g_p(v,N_p)=0$, so the definition is exhaustive and
mutually exclusive. Replacing $N$ by $-N$ reverses every future/past label, and
two time orientations $N,N'$ determine the same future-directed causal vectors
at every point where $g_p(N_p,N'_p)<0$, while they determine opposite ones
where $g_p(N_p,N'_p)>0$, by
[[lem-gr-timelike-fields-define-equal-or-opposite-future-cones]]; that lemma
also shows the sign of $p\mapsto g_p(N_p,N'_p)$ is constant on every connected
component of $M$.

**(d) The inverse metric.** Because $g_p$ is nondegenerate, it induces at each
$p$ an isomorphism $\flat_p:T_pM\to T_p^*M$, $v\mapsto g_p(v,\cdot)$, and an
inverse metric $g_p^{-1}$ on the dual space; the inverse metric, the musical
isomorphisms and the components $g^{ab}$ are defined separately on this page,
where the smoothness of those components is also proved. Neither construction
uses any choice principle beyond the one already recorded in (c).


**(e) Smooth timelike curves and their scalar normalization.** Before using
these quantities in the physical conventions, fix a positive real scaling
parameter $c$ (with no physical meaning or dimension in this mathematical
item). A **smooth future timelike curve** is a smooth map $\gamma:I\to M$
from a nonempty open real interval $I$ ([[def-interval]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]) whose velocity derivation
$\gamma'(s)\in T_{\gamma(s)}M$
([[def-velocity-derivation-of-a-smooth-curve]]) satisfies
$g(\gamma',\gamma')<0$ and $g(\gamma',N)<0$ at every $s\in I$.
In a chart its components are $d(x^a\circ\gamma)/ds$, $a=0,1,2,3$.
For a supplied base point $s_0\in I$ and additive constant $\tau_0\in\mathbb R$
define

$$h(s):=\sqrt{-g_{\gamma(s)}(\gamma'(s),\gamma'(s))},\qquad \tau(s):=\tau_0+\frac1c\int_{s_0}^{s}h(r)\,dr,\qquad U(s):=\frac{c\gamma'(s)}{h(s)}.$$

The integral is oriented when $s<s_0$. The function $\tau$ is called
**proper time** for this scaling and $U$ the **four-velocity** of the smooth
curve; its increment times $c$ is the Lorentzian length. The well-definedness
proof below shows $\tau'>0$, that $\tau:I\to\tau(I)$ is a smooth
diffeomorphism, and that $U$ is the velocity of $\gamma\circ\tau^{-1}$.
Thus $g(U,U)=-c^2$ and $U$ is future timelike. This introduces the smooth
case before any physical unit reading; the later worldline definition extends
it to its stated $C^k$, endpoint and piecewise-$C^1$ classes. It asserts no
clock coupling, motion law or physical value of $c$.

**Convention and scope.** The physical reading of a smooth time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold as a classical spacetime model, and the domain in which
that reading is adopted, are recorded in the framework postulate
`post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain`; the words spacetime and event carry no
mathematical content beyond this definition, and this item asserts no claim
about nature. The dimension $4$ and the absence of boundary are part of the
data; nothing in the definition assumes that $M$ is nonempty or connected, and
no completeness, extendibility or maximality property of $(M,g)$ is asserted.

A **smooth $n$-manifold** is a pair $(M,\mathcal S)$ in which $M$ is a
topological $n$-manifold
([[def-topological-manifold-without-boundary]]) and $\mathcal S$ is a **smooth
structure** on $M$: a maximal smooth atlas
([[thm-each-smooth-atlas-is-contained-in-a-unique-maximal-smooth-atlas]]).
Because
[[thm-each-smooth-atlas-is-contained-in-a-unique-maximal-smooth-atlas]] sends
every smooth atlas to the unique maximal atlas containing it, a smooth manifold
is equivalently specified by a topological manifold $M$ together with any one
smooth atlas $\mathcal A$, the structure being the generated $[\mathcal A]$. A
chart $(U,\varphi)\in\mathcal S$ is called a **smooth chart** (or a **chart of
the smooth structure**); its domain is a **coordinate domain** and its
coordinate functions are **smooth coordinates** on $U$. When the structure is
clear from context, the manifold itself is written $M$ in place of
$(M,\mathcal S)$.

Let $a \in \mathbb{R}$, where $\mathbb{R}$ is the ambient ordered field
(Ordered field, Field).

**Natural exponents.** By the recursion theorem (The recursion theorem) applied to
the set $\mathbb{R}$, the starting element $1$ and the function
$f(x) = x \cdot a$, there is a unique function $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$,
written $n \mapsto a^n$, with

$$a^0 = 1, \qquad a^{n+1} = a^n \cdot a \quad (n \in \mathbb{N}).$$

Thus $a^1 = a$, $a^2 = a \cdot a$, and so on. Note that this is defined for
**every** $a$, including $a = 0$.

**Negative exponents.** If $a \ne 0$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$ with $n \ge 1$, set

$$a^{-n} := (a^n)^{-1}.$$

**Why that is legitimate.** The right-hand side presupposes that $a^n$ is
invertible, that is, that $a^n \ne 0$. This is a proof obligation and not an
observation, and it is discharged by claim 2 of Laws of integer exponents: for $a \ne 0$
in a field, $a^n \ne 0$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, proved there by induction on
$n$ from the fact that a field has no zero divisors (A field has no zero divisors: $ab = 0 \Rightarrow a = 0$ or $b = 0$).
That lemma is a statement *about* the operation introduced here, so it depends on
this definition and is recorded in this item's `justified_by` rather than in its
`deps` (SCHEMA §3). Given $a^n \ne 0$, the value $(a^n)^{-1}$ is a single
well-determined element, because multiplicative inverses in a field are unique
(Identities and inverses in a field are unique).

**Integer exponents.** Every integer $m$ (The integers as equivalence classes of pairs of naturals) is either
$n$ or $-n$ for a unique natural $n$, where $n$ in these integer expressions denotes its image under the
embedding $\iota : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}$ (The naturals embed in the integers,
Arithmetic on the integers). This too is a citation and not a slogan: the order on
$\mathbb{Z}$ is total (The integers form a totally ordered ring), so $m \ge 0$ or $m < 0$; the
image of $\iota$ is exactly the set of nonnegative integers, and each of them is
$n$ for a unique natural $n$ (The naturals embed in the integers); and if $m < 0$ then
$-m > 0$, by compatibility of the order with addition (The integers form a totally ordered ring),
so $-m = n$ and $m = -n$, with $n$ unique because $\iota$ is
injective. The two clauses above therefore define $a^m$ for every
$m \in \mathbb{Z}$ whenever $a \ne 0$, and for every $m \in \mathbb{N}$ for
arbitrary $a$. The two exponent domains are disjoint: the natural clause
handles $m \ge 0$, including $m = 0$, while the negative clause requires
$n \ge 1$ and therefore handles only $m < 0$.

Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, let $c \in A$ be a limit point of $A$
(Limit point, isolated point, adherent point, derived set, and dense subset of $\mathbb{R}$), let $f, g : A \to \mathbb{R}$ be differentiable at $c$
(The derivative $f'(c) = \lim_{x \to c} \frac{f(x) - f(c)}{x - c}$ of $f : A \to \mathbb{R}$ at a point $c \in A$ that is a limit point of $A$, and differentiability on a set) and let $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$. Then:

1. $f + g$ is differentiable at $c$ and $(f+g)'(c) = f'(c) + g'(c)$;
2. $\alpha f$ is differentiable at $c$ and $(\alpha f)'(c) = \alpha f'(c)$;
3. $fg$ is differentiable at $c$ and $(fg)'(c) = f'(c)g(c) + f(c)g'(c)$;
4. if $g(c) \ne 0$ then, writing $A_0 := \{\, x \in A : g(x) \ne 0 \,\}$, the
   point $c$ lies in $A_0$ and is a limit point of $A_0$, the quotient
   $(f/g)|_{A_0} : A_0 \to \mathbb{R}$, $x \mapsto f(x)/g(x)$, is differentiable
   at $c$ as a function on $A_0$, and
   $$\bigl((f/g)|_{A_0}\bigr)'(c) \;=\; \frac{f'(c)\,g(c) - f(c)\,g'(c)}{g(c)^{2}} .$$

Each claim asserts two things: that the derivative on the left exists, and that
it has the stated value. Both are proved.

**Why claim 4 is stated on $A_0$.** The function $f/g$ is not defined where $g$
vanishes, and $g$ may vanish at points of $A$ far from $c$; restricting to $A_0$
is forced. That the restriction still has $c$ as a limit point, so that a
derivative there means anything at all, is not free either, and it is the last
claim of If $\lim_{x \to c} f(x) = L \ne 0$ then $|f| > |L|/2$ on a punctured neighbourhood of $c$; in particular if $L > 0$ then $f > L/2 > 0$ there applied to $g$. The hypothesis
is $g(c) \ne 0$, not "$g$ vanishes nowhere".

**Everything is proved through
Carathéodory's characterisation: $f$ is differentiable at $c$ if and only if there is $\varphi : A \to \mathbb{R}$, continuous at $c$, with $f(x) - f(c) = \varphi(x)(x - c)$ for every $x \in A$, and then $\varphi$ is unique and $\varphi(c) = f'(c)$.** No difference quotient is estimated and
no limit theorem beyond continuity is used, so no choice principle is spent.
The four identities are four algebraic rearrangements of an increment, each
followed by a reading of Sums, scalar multiples, products, absolute values, maxima, minima and quotients with nonvanishing denominator of continuous functions are continuous, as are constants, the identity and every polynomial function.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $M$, $N$, $P$ be smooth manifolds.

1. The identity map $\mathrm{id}_M:M\to M$ is smooth.
2. If $F:M\to N$ and $G:N\to P$ are smooth, then $G\circ F:M\to P$ is smooth.

In coordinates for a Riemannian metric with matrix $(g_{ij})$ and inverse $(g^{ij})$, its Levi–Civita symbols are
$$\Gamma^k{}_{ij}=\tfrac12\sum_\ell g^{k\ell}(\partial_i g_{j\ell}+\partial_j g_{i\ell}-\partial_\ell g_{ij}).$$

Christoffel symbols of a smooth Riemannian metric are
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12 g^{ad}(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc})$.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $\nabla$ be an affine connection on a smooth manifold $M$. For $p\in M$
and $u,v,w\in T_pM$, choose smooth local extensions $X,Y,Z$ and set

$$R_p(u,v)w:=(R(X,Y)Z)_p.$$

This is independent of the extensions, is trilinear in $(u,v,w)$, and varies
smoothly with $p$. Equivalently,

$$\mathcal R_p(\alpha,u,v,w):=\alpha\bigl(R_p(u,v)w\bigr)$$

is a smooth type $(1,3)$ tensor field. We use $R$ for both this tensor and its
vector-valued representative.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $T$ be a type $(r,s)$ tensor on $V$ with $r,s\ge 1$. Contracting the first
contravariant slot against the first covariant slot gives the type
$(r-1,s-1)$ tensor $\operatorname{ctr}(T)$ defined intrinsically by

$$ \operatorname{ctr}(T)(\alpha_2,\ldots,\alpha_r,v_2,\ldots,v_s) :=\sum_i T(e^i,\alpha_2,\ldots,\alpha_r,e_i,v_2,\ldots,v_s), $$

where $(e_i)$ is any basis of $V$ and $(e^i)$ its dual basis. The next lemma
shows that this formula is basis-independent.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$ and Einstein tensor $G$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]), let
$\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a spacelike embedded hypersurface
([[def-embedded-submanifold-and-slice-chart]],
[[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (a)), and fix real
constants $\kappa$ and $\Lambda$ (the framework coupling constants, purely
parameters for this definition).

**(a) The geometric data.**
For $p\in\Sigma$ the orthogonal complement $T_p\Sigma^{\perp}$ is
one-dimensional and nondegenerate
([[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]],
[[lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis]]); there is therefore a unique
$n_p\in T_p\Sigma^{\perp}$ with $g_p(n_p,n_p)=-1$ and $g_p(n_p,N_p)<0$ and it
depends smoothly on $p$, the **future unit normal field** of $\Sigma$; this
and the properties of $h$ and $K$ below are proved, not assumed, in
[[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]. Define
on $\Sigma$ the **induced metric** $h$ and the **second fundamental form**
$K$ by
$$h_p(V,W):=g_p(V,W),\qquad K_p(V,W):=g_p(\nabla_Vn,W)\qquad(V,W\in T_p\Sigma),$$
where $\nabla_Vn$ is the covariant derivative at $p$ of the ambient field $n$
in the tangential direction $V$; $h$ is a smooth Riemannian metric on
$\Sigma$ and $K$ a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $\Sigma$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]).

**(b) Matter data and constraints.** Let $T$ be a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field on $M$ (the stress-energy field of a matter branch). Its
**matter data on $\Sigma$** are the smooth fields
$$\rho:=T(n,n),\qquad j(V):=-T(n,V)\quad(V\in T\Sigma).$$
The tuple $(\Sigma,h,K,\rho,j)$ **satisfies the constraint equations** for
$(\kappa,\Lambda)$ when
$$G(n,n)-\Lambda=\kappa\,\rho,\qquad G(n,V)=\kappa\,T(n,V)\quad\text{for every }V\in T_p\Sigma,\ p\in\Sigma .$$
The first is the normal projection of the equation $G+\Lambda g=\kappa T$
evaluated on $(n,n)$, namely $G(n,n)+\Lambda g(n,n)=\kappa T(n,n)$, with
$g(n,n)=-1$; the second is the normal-tangential projection, the term in
$\Lambda$ dropping because $g(n,V)=0$. That a solution of the field equation
satisfies these two projections is proved in
[[lem-gr-constraint-projections]]. The purely tangential projection
$G(V,W)+\Lambda h(V,W)=\kappa T(V,W)$ is not part of the constraints and is
not required here.

**(c) Developments.** A **development** of the data
$(\Sigma,h,K,\rho,j)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
$(M',g',N')$ together with a smooth embedding $\varphi:\Sigma\to M'$ whose
image is a spacelike embedded hypersurface with induced metric $\varphi^*g'=h$
and second fundamental form $K$ with respect to its future unit normal $n'$.
Write $T'$ for the smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field included as
the development's stress-energy field. Require the tensor equation
$$G'+\Lambda g'=\kappa T'$$
at every point of $M'$, where $G'$ is the Einstein tensor of $g'$ with its
metric-selected connection, defined as above. The constants $\kappa$ and
$\Lambda$ are the fixed parameters of the initial data. The matter-data matching condition is
the pair of normal projections
$$\rho(p)=T'_{\varphi(p)}(n'_{\varphi(p)},n'_{\varphi(p)}),\qquad j_p(V)=-T'_{\varphi(p)}(n'_{\varphi(p)},d\varphi_p(V))\quad(p\in\Sigma,\ V\in T_p\Sigma).$$
Equivalently, the scalar field $T'(n',n')$ along $\varphi(\Sigma)$ pulls
back to $\rho$, and the covector field $-T'(n',\cdot)$ restricted to
$T\varphi(\Sigma)$ pulls back to $j$. This tuple prescribes only these
stress-energy projections; any additional matter-field data are not included
in $(\Sigma,h,K,\rho,j)$. The development is a **globally hyperbolic
development** when
$\varphi(\Sigma)$ is a Cauchy hypersurface of $(M',g',N')$. The implication
from this Cauchy property to global hyperbolicity of $(M',g',N')$ is a
separate theorem, deferred to the later causal theory; it is not established
by this definition
([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]],
[[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (c)).

**(d) Maximality.** A globally hyperbolic development $(M_*,g_*,N_*;
\varphi_*)$ is **maximal** for the data when for every globally hyperbolic
development $(M',g',N';\varphi')$ there is a smooth isometric embedding
$\psi:M'\to M_*$ with $\psi\circ\varphi'=\varphi_*$, $\psi$ preserving the
time orientations and carrying the selected stress-energy tensor $T'$ to
$T_*$, that is, $\psi^*T_*=T'$. This is a universal embedding property: every globally hyperbolic
development embeds into the selected maximal one with its data and
stress-energy tensor preserved. It does not assert that arbitrary globally
hyperbolic developments are mutually isometric.

**(e) Scope.** The definition asserts neither existence nor uniqueness of
developments, and it does not assert that $T'$ is generated by matter fields
solving any equation: those claims require the local and global existence theory of
the Einstein-matter system and are not made on this page. The constraint
equations are displayed only as equations satisfied or not by given data.
The equivalent formulation of the constraints in terms of the induced scalar
curvature of $h$ and the divergence of $K$, and the existence theory for
solutions of the constraints, rest on the Gauss-Codazzi relations and on PDE
theory and are deferred to the later pages of this track; no such
equivalence is asserted here.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, and let $\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a smooth spacelike embedded hypersurface with future unit normal $n$, induced Riemannian metric $h$ and second fundamental form $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_Xn,Y)$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]], [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]). Write $D$ for the Levi-Civita connection of $h$, $R^h$ for its curvature operator in the same operator convention as the ambient curvature, and $S_h$ for its scalar curvature. Explicitly distinguish the lowered tensor from the operator pairing by setting
$$\mathcal R^g(A,B,C,D):=g(R^g(C,D)B,A),\qquad \mathcal R^h(A,B,C,D):=h(R^h(C,D)B,A).$$
Thus $\mathcal R^g_{abcd}=R_{abcd}$ in [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]; in particular $g(R^g(X,Y)Z,W)=\mathcal R^g(W,Z,X,Y)$. Let $G$ be the Einstein tensor defined there. At every $p\in\Sigma$ and for all $X,Y,Z,W\in T_p\Sigma$:

**(a) Gauss equation.**
$$\mathcal R^g(X,Y,Z,W)=\mathcal R^h(X,Y,Z,W)+K(X,Z)K(Y,W)-K(X,W)K(Y,Z).$$
Equivalently, in operator order,
$$g(R^g(X,Y)Z,W)=h(R^h(X,Y)Z,W)+K(Y,Z)K(X,W)-K(X,Z)K(Y,W).$$

**(b) Codazzi equation.**
$$g(R^g(X,Y)Z,n)=(D_YK)(X,Z)-(D_XK)(Y,Z).$$

**(c) Normal projections.** Define $(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)=h^{ij}(D_{e_i}K)(e_j,Y)$, $\tau=\operatorname{tr}_hK=h^{ij}K_{ij}$ and $|K|_h^2=h^{ik}h^{jl}K_{ij}K_{kl}$. Then
$$G(n,n)=\tfrac12(S_h+\tau^2-|K|_h^2),\qquad G(n,Y)=(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau.$$

**(d) Constraint equations.** If the tensor equation $G+\Lambda g=\kappa T$ holds at $p$, for a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor $T$ and real constants $\kappa,\Lambda$, then
$$S_h+\tau^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T(n,n),\qquad (\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau=\kappa T(n,Y).$$
With $\rho=T(n,n)$ and $j(Y)=-T(n,Y)$, the second equation is $(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau=-\kappa j(Y)$.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Let $\Sigma$ be a nonempty compact smooth three-manifold without boundary. In
this item, “vacuum” means that the stress-energy tensor is zero and the
cosmological constant is fixed at $\Lambda=0$. Let $\widetilde h$ be a smooth
Riemannian metric on $\Sigma$, let $\widetilde\sigma$ be a smooth symmetric
covariant two-tensor field, let $\tau\in\mathbb R$ be constant, and let
$\phi\in C^\infty(\Sigma,\mathbb R)$ satisfy $\phi(p)>0$ at every $p\in\Sigma$.
Use the positive scalar $\phi$ as a dimensionless conformal factor.

Write $\widetilde D$ for the Levi-Civita connection of $\widetilde h$ and
$D$ for that of the metric $h$ defined below. On covariant tensor fields, these
symbols also denote their induced product connections, with the dual and
tensor-factor rules of [[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]].
In a chart, $\widetilde h^{ij}$
denotes the inverse matrix to $\widetilde h_{ij}$. It is smooth because
$\det(\widetilde h_{ij})>0$ and the matrix inverse is the adjugate divided by
the determinant. For any smooth Riemannian metric $m$ on $\Sigma$, with
Levi-Civita connection $D^m$, define
$$R^m(X,Y)Z:=D^m_XD^m_YZ-D^m_YD^m_XZ-D^m_{[X,Y]}Z.$$
In a chart, $R[m]^a{}_{bij}$ denotes the components of
$R^m(\partial_i,\partial_j)\partial_b$. Define
$\operatorname{Ric}(m)_{ij}:=R[m]^k{}_{ikj}$ and
$R(m):=m^{ij}\operatorname{Ric}(m)_{ij}$. In particular,
$\widetilde R:=R(\widetilde h)$, with the same curvature sign convention.
Define the scalar Laplacian by
$$\widetilde\Delta f:=\widetilde h^{ij} (\partial_i\partial_j f-\widetilde\Gamma^k{}_{ij}\partial_k f),$$
where $\widetilde\Gamma^k{}_{ij}$ are the Christoffel symbols of
$\widetilde D$, given by the Levi-Civita Christoffel formula
[[prop-christoffel-formula-for-the-levi-civita-connection]].
The curvature sign is the one displayed above. All traces, norms, raising of
indices and contractions in this item use the metric indicated by the
subscript. In particular,
$$\operatorname{tr}_{\widetilde h}\widetilde\sigma:=\widetilde h^{ij}\widetilde\sigma_{ij},\qquad |\widetilde\sigma|_{\widetilde h}^2:=\widetilde h^{ik}\widetilde h^{j\ell}\widetilde\sigma_{ij}\widetilde\sigma_{k\ell},\qquad (\operatorname{div}_{\widetilde h}\widetilde\sigma)_j:=\widetilde h^{ik}\widetilde D_i\widetilde\sigma_{kj}.$$
The tensor $\widetilde\sigma$ is **transverse-traceless** (TT) with respect
to $\widetilde h$ when it is symmetric and both displayed trace and divergence
vanish. The input tensor in this definition is required to be TT.

Define
$$h:=\phi^4\widetilde h,\qquad K:=\phi^{-2}\widetilde\sigma+\frac{\tau}{3}h.$$
Because $\phi>0$, $h$ is a smooth Riemannian metric; because
$\widetilde\sigma$ and $h$ are symmetric, $K$ is a smooth symmetric tensor.
Here $h$ is the candidate induced Riemannian metric and $K$ is the candidate
second fundamental form, with the library convention
$K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_X n,Y)$ when the data are induced by a spacelike hypersurface
with future unit normal $n$. The pair is **vacuum conformal constraint data**.
It is abstract data on $\Sigma$; no embedding into a spacetime is part of this
definition. For its embedded Lorentzian interpretation assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, as in the supplied smooth tangent-bundle
convention; the algebraic tensor definitions themselves use no choice
principle. Define the $h$-trace, squared norm and divergence by
$$\operatorname{tr}_hK:=h^{ij}K_{ij},\qquad |K|_h^2:=h^{ik}h^{j\ell}K_{ij}K_{k\ell},\qquad (\operatorname{div}_hK)_j:=h^{ik}D_iK_{kj}.$$
With $R(h)$ computed using $h$, define the Hamiltonian and momentum residuals
$$\mathcal H(h,K):=R(h)+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|_h^2,\qquad \mathcal M_j(h,K):=h^{ik}D_iK_{kj}-D_j(\operatorname{tr}_hK).$$
The data satisfy the vacuum constraint equations when
$\mathcal H(h,K)=0$ and $\mathcal M(h,K)=0$. For an embedded hypersurface,
these are the normal and normal-tangential Einstein constraints in the
specified $K$ convention.

Tensoriality of curvature and basis-independent contraction make these scalar
curvatures independent of the chart.
For dimensional bookkeeping in the SI length convention, $[\tau]=\mathrm m^{-1}$,
$[R(h)]=[\widetilde R]=[|\widetilde\sigma|_{\widetilde h}^2]
=[\widetilde\Delta]=\mathrm m^{-2}$, and $[\phi]=1$. Thus all terms in the
scalar constraint equation have units $\mathrm m^{-2}$.
