citations.quote:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the tangent-bundle smooth structure of the
Lorentzian conventions.

Let $M>0$ and $a\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $|a|<M$, and put
$r_\pm:=M\pm\sqrt{M^2-a^2}$.

Let $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}:=\mathbb R\times(r_+,\infty)\times S^2$ carry the
product smooth structure, where $S^2=\{(x,y,z)\in\mathbb R^3:x^2+y^2+z^2=1\}$
has its usual smooth structure and round metric $\gamma_{S^2}$. Let
$\pi:\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}\to S^2$ be the third projection, let $\xi$ be the
smooth rotation field on $S^2$ generated by $(x,y,z)\mapsto(-y,x,0)$, and put
$\gamma:=\pi^*\gamma_{S^2}$ and
$\xi^\flat:=\pi^*(\gamma_{S^2}(\xi,\cdot))$. Let $t,r$ be the first and
second coordinate functions on $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}$, and let
$\zeta:=z\circ\pi$ be the third Euclidean coordinate on the sphere factor.
Define the global smooth functions

$$\Sigma:=r^2+a^2\zeta^2,\qquad \Delta:=r^2-2Mr+a^2.$$

On a polar chart $0<\theta<\pi$, $\phi\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$, one has
$\zeta=\cos\theta$, $\Sigma=r^2+a^2\cos^2\theta$,
$\gamma=d\theta^2+\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2$, and
$\xi^\flat=\sin^2\theta\,d\phi$.

Define the symmetric covariant $2$-tensor $g$ globally on $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}$
by

$$g=-\left(1-\frac{2Mr}{\Sigma}\right)dt\otimes dt+\frac{\Sigma}{\Delta}\,dr\otimes dr+\Sigma\gamma+\frac{a^2(\Sigma+2Mr)}{\Sigma}\,\xi^\flat\otimes\xi^\flat-\frac{2aMr}{\Sigma}\left(dt\otimes\xi^\flat+\xi^\flat\otimes dt\right).$$

Its Boyer-Lindquist line element on the polar chart is

$$ds^2=-\left(1-\frac{2Mr}{\Sigma}\right)dt^2-\frac{4Mar\sin^2\theta}{\Sigma}\,dt\,d\phi+\frac{\Sigma}{\Delta}\,dr^2+\Sigma\,d\theta^2+\frac{(r^2+a^2)^2-a^2\Delta\sin^2\theta}{\Sigma}\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2.$$

The displayed cross term is $2g_{t\phi}\,dt\,d\phi$. This definition makes
no nondegeneracy or signature claim; Lorentzian signature and a time orientation
are established separately.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). The cotangent space $T_p^*M$ is
the algebraic dual of $T_pM$ ([[def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional]]).

**Musical isomorphisms.** Define the **flat map**

$$\flat_p:T_pM\longrightarrow T_p^*M,\qquad \flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot),$$

so that $\flat_p(v)(w)=g_p(v,w)$; it is $\mathbb R$-linear by bilinearity of
$g_p$. Its kernel is $\{v:g_p(v,w)=0\text{ for all }w\}=\{0\}$ because $g_p$ is
nondegenerate, and $\dim_{\mathbb R}T_pM=\dim_{\mathbb R}T_p^*M=4$ since the
coordinate derivations of a chart form a basis of $T_pM$
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]); hence
$\flat_p$ is a linear isomorphism and has an inverse
$\sharp_p:T_p^*M\to T_pM$.

**Inverse metric.** The **inverse metric** at $p$ is the symmetric bilinear form

$$g_p^{-1}:T_p^*M\times T_p^*M\longrightarrow\mathbb R,\qquad g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta).$$

It is symmetric because $g_p$ is, and it is nondegenerate: if
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta)=0$ for all $\beta$, then $g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\cdot)=0$,
so $\sharp_p\alpha=0$ and hence $\alpha=0$.

**Components in a chart.** Let $(U,x)$ be a smooth chart and
$g_{ab}(q)=g_q(\partial_a|_q,\partial_b|_q)$ the components of $g$; let
$dx^a|_q$ be the differential of the coordinate function $x^a$ at $q$
([[def-differential-of-a-smooth-map]]), so that
$dx^a|_q(\partial_b|_q)=\partial_b|_q(x^a)=\delta^a{}_b$. Define the components
of the inverse metric in this chart by

$$g^{ab}(q):=g_q^{-1}\bigl(dx^a|_q,\,dx^b|_q\bigr),\qquad q\in U,$$

so that $\sharp_q(dx^a|_q)=\sum_bg^{ab}(q)\,\partial_b|_q$; equivalently
$(g^{ab}(q))$ is the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab}(q))$ at every $q$, that is

$$g^{ac}(q)\,g_{cb}(q)=\delta^a{}_b,\qquad g_{ac}(q)g^{cb}(q)=\delta_a{}^b,$$

because $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=dx^a|_q(\partial_c|_q)=\delta^a{}_c$
and also $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=\sum_bg^{ab}(q)g_{bc}(q)$. In
particular $g^{ab}=g^{ba}$. The components $g^{ab}$ depend smoothly on $q$;
this is proved in [[lem-gr-inverse-metric-is-smooth]].

**Raising, lowering and metric trace.** Let $A$ be a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field on an open set $V\subseteq M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). At each $p\in V$ define the
endomorphism

$$A^\sharp_p:T_pM\to T_pM,\qquad A^\sharp_p(v):=\sharp_p\bigl(A_p(v,\cdot)\bigr),$$

characterized by $g_p(A^\sharp_p(v),w)=A_p(v,w)$ for all $w\in T_pM$; it is
self-adjoint for $g_p$ because $A_p$ is symmetric. Its **metric trace** is

$$\operatorname{tr}_g(A)(p):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(A^\sharp_p\bigr)$$

with the trace of an endomorphism as in [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. In a
chart the raised, mixed and doubly raised components are

$$A^{ab}:=g^{ac}g^{bd}A_{cd},\qquad A^a{}_b:=g^{ac}A_{cb},\qquad\text{and}\qquad \operatorname{tr}_g(A)=g^{ab}A_{ab},$$

the last identity obtained by evaluating in a $g_p$-orthonormal basis
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$, where $g_p(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ by
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]] so that
$g^{ab}A_{ab}=\sum_a g^{aa}A_{aa}=-A(e_0,e_0)+A(e_1,e_1)+A(e_2,e_2)+A(e_3,e_3)$,
which is the trace of the endomorphism $v\mapsto\sharp_p(A_p(v,\cdot))$ in that
basis. All these operations are pointwise and depend only on $g$, $A$ and the
duality pairing, not on a chart.

**Conventions.** Raising and lowering apply to one index at a time and preserve
index order; $A_{ab}$, $A^a{}_b$ and $A^{ab}$ denote the same tensor $A$ with
indices positioned by $g$. The musical isomorphisms and the inverse metric are
defined for every smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of this library; no choice
principle is used in this definition, every ingredient being pointwise linear
algebra over $\mathbb R$ together with the pointwise nondegeneracy of $g_p$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$g_p^{-1}$ and $g^{ab}$ be the inverse metric and its chart components as in
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]. Then:

1. For every smooth chart $(U,x)$ the component functions $g^{ab}:U\to\mathbb R$
   are $C^\infty$ on $U$.
2. For overlapping smooth charts $(U,x)$, $(V,y)$ the components satisfy the
   contravariant transformation law

$$g'^{ab}(u)=\sum_{c,d=0}^{3}\frac{\partial y^a}{\partial x^c}\bigl(x(u)\bigr)\, \frac{\partial y^b}{\partial x^d}\bigl(x(u)\bigr)\,g^{cd}\bigl(x(u)\bigr),\qquad u\in y(U\cap V),$$

where every component evaluated at a coordinate tuple is its coordinate
representative, as in [[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]],
$x(u)$ denotes $(x\circ y^{-1})(u)$, and $\partial y^a/\partial x^c$ are
the entries of $D(y\circ x^{-1})$.

3. Consequently the pointwise bilinear forms $g_p^{-1}$ on $T_p^*M$ are
   presented by component functions that are smooth in every chart and glue by
   the contravariant law; the inverse metric is a well-defined smooth component
   family determined by $g$ alone.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary, so that $M$ is Hausdorff
and second countable and carries a maximal smooth atlas
([[def-smooth-manifold]]). Let $g$ be a smooth covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$
in the sense of [[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]. Then $g$ assigns
to every $p\in M$ a bilinear form $g_p:T_pM\times T_pM\to\mathbb R$
([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]).

**(a) Lorentzian metric.** The field $g$ is a **Lorentzian metric of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$** on $M$ when it is symmetric and nondegenerate, and at every
$p\in M$ the pair $(T_pM,g_p)$ is a Lorentz vector space of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ in the sense of [[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]: that is, $g_p$ has
inertia $(3,1,0)$, so that some — equivalently every — basis of $T_pM$ in which
the matrix of $g_p$ is diagonal has exactly one negative and three positive
diagonal entries. The pair $(M,g)$ is a **smooth Lorentzian four-manifold** (or
Lorentzian manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$). In a smooth chart $(U,x)$ the
**components** of $g$ are the $C^\infty$ functions
$g_{ab}(q)=g_q(\partial_a|_q,\partial_b|_q)$ of
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]], and $g_{ab}=g_{ba}$ by symmetry.
We use indices $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$ and the Einstein summation convention, with
components in a chart written as lower-case indexed symbols and equations
between indexed fields understood basis-independently. These conventions are
fixed once for this library and the physical reading of the symbols is recorded
with the framework postulates, separately from this mathematical definition.

**(b) Pointwise causal structure.** For every $p\in M$ the vocabulary of
[[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] applies to the Lorentz vector
space $(T_pM,g_p)$: a tangent vector $v\in T_pM$ is **timelike** when
$g_p(v,v)<0$, **null** when $v\neq0$ and $g_p(v,v)=0$, **spacelike** when
$g_p(v,v)>0$, and **causal** when it is timelike or null. Every nonzero
$v\in T_pM$ has exactly one causal character. The **timelike set**
$T_p:=\{v\in T_pM:g_p(v,v)<0\}$ has exactly two connected components, each
nonempty, open, convex and path-connected; each $g_p$-orthonormal basis
$e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3$ of $T_pM$ satisfies $g_p(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$
for some ordering, so in particular nonzero orthonormal vectors exist at every
point ([[lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis]],
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]]).

**(c) Time orientation.** A **time orientation** of $(M,g)$, also called a
**choice of future cone**, is a smooth vector field $N$ on $M$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]], whose tangent-bundle
smooth structure uses the axiom $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of
[[def-countable-choice]]; this is the only use of that axiom in this
definition) such that

$$g_p(N_p,N_p)<0\qquad\text{for every }p\in M .$$

The function $p\mapsto g_p(N_p,N_p)$ is $C^\infty$ because $g$ is a smooth
covariant $2$-tensor field and $N$ a smooth field, so the condition is a
pointwise strict inequality between a smooth function and $0$; since
$g_p(N_p,N_p)<0$ implies $N_p\neq0$, a time orientation is nowhere vanishing.
A **time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold** is a triple $(M,g,N)$
consisting of a smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and a time orientation $N$.

Given a time orientation $N$ and $p\in M$, the vector $N_p$ is timelike, and we
**define** a nonzero causal vector $v\in T_pM$ to be **future-directed** when
$g_p(v,N_p)<0$ and **past-directed** when $g_p(v,N_p)>0$. The classification of
nonzero causal vectors into exactly these two classes, and its agreement with
the two components of the timelike set (the future component is the component
$C_p^+$ containing $N_p$, and the future causal vectors form
$\operatorname{cl}(C_p^+)\setminus\{0\}$), is proved in
[[lem-gr-future-causal-classification-by-a-timelike-field]]; in particular no
nonzero causal $v$ satisfies $g_p(v,N_p)=0$, so the definition is exhaustive and
mutually exclusive. Replacing $N$ by $-N$ reverses every future/past label, and
two time orientations $N,N'$ determine the same future-directed causal vectors
at every point where $g_p(N_p,N'_p)<0$, while they determine opposite ones
where $g_p(N_p,N'_p)>0$, by
[[lem-gr-timelike-fields-define-equal-or-opposite-future-cones]]; that lemma
also shows the sign of $p\mapsto g_p(N_p,N'_p)$ is constant on every connected
component of $M$.

**(d) The inverse metric.** Because $g_p$ is nondegenerate, it induces at each
$p$ an isomorphism $\flat_p:T_pM\to T_p^*M$, $v\mapsto g_p(v,\cdot)$, and an
inverse metric $g_p^{-1}$ on the dual space; the inverse metric, the musical
isomorphisms and the components $g^{ab}$ are defined separately on this page,
where the smoothness of those components is also proved. Neither construction
uses any choice principle beyond the one already recorded in (c).


**(e) Smooth timelike curves and their scalar normalization.** Before using
these quantities in the physical conventions, fix a positive real scaling
parameter $c$ (with no physical meaning or dimension in this mathematical
item). A **smooth future timelike curve** is a smooth map $\gamma:I\to M$
from a nonempty open real interval $I$ ([[def-interval]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]) whose velocity derivation
$\gamma'(s)\in T_{\gamma(s)}M$
([[def-velocity-derivation-of-a-smooth-curve]]) satisfies
$g(\gamma',\gamma')<0$ and $g(\gamma',N)<0$ at every $s\in I$.
In a chart its components are $d(x^a\circ\gamma)/ds$, $a=0,1,2,3$.
For a supplied base point $s_0\in I$ and additive constant $\tau_0\in\mathbb R$
define

$$h(s):=\sqrt{-g_{\gamma(s)}(\gamma'(s),\gamma'(s))},\qquad \tau(s):=\tau_0+\frac1c\int_{s_0}^{s}h(r)\,dr,\qquad U(s):=\frac{c\gamma'(s)}{h(s)}.$$

The integral is oriented when $s<s_0$. The function $\tau$ is called
**proper time** for this scaling and $U$ the **four-velocity** of the smooth
curve; its increment times $c$ is the Lorentzian length. The well-definedness
proof below shows $\tau'>0$, that $\tau:I\to\tau(I)$ is a smooth
diffeomorphism, and that $U$ is the velocity of $\gamma\circ\tau^{-1}$.
Thus $g(U,U)=-c^2$ and $U$ is future timelike. This introduces the smooth
case before any physical unit reading; the later worldline definition extends
it to its stated $C^k$, endpoint and piecewise-$C^1$ classes. It asserts no
clock coupling, motion law or physical value of $c$.

**Convention and scope.** The physical reading of a smooth time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold as a classical spacetime model, and the domain in which
that reading is adopted, are recorded in the framework postulate
`post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain`; the words spacetime and event carry no
mathematical content beyond this definition, and this item asserts no claim
about nature. The dimension $4$ and the absence of boundary are part of the
data; nothing in the definition assumes that $M$ is nonempty or connected, and
no completeness, extendibility or maximality property of $(M,g)$ is asserted.

For $a>0$, the function $x\mapsto a^x$ is continuous on $\mathbb R$ and
$$(a^x)'=a^x\log a.$$
For $\alpha\in\mathbb R$, the function $x\mapsto x^\alpha$ is continuous and differentiable on $(0,\infty)$, with
$$(x^\alpha)'=\alpha x^{\alpha-1}.$$

Let $k\in\mathbb N$. Finite componentwise sums and products of $C^k$ Euclidean maps are $C^k$, and a composite of composable $C^k$ Euclidean maps is $C^k$. Scalar multiples are included among the finite componentwise operations. The assertions remain valid on an empty open domain.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, so that $TM$ carries its canonical smooth
structure. Let $M$ be a smooth manifold. A **smooth vector field** on $M$ is a
smooth section

$$ X:M\to TM $$

of the tangent-bundle projection $\pi:TM\to M$. Thus $\pi\circ X=\operatorname{id}_M$.

Equivalently, for each $p\in M$ the value $X(p)$ is a tangent vector in $T_pM$,
and the dependence on $p$ is smooth with respect to the canonical smooth
structure on $TM$.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

derivations.claim: Since $0<\sqrt{M^2-a^2}\le M$, with equality in the upper bound exactly when $a=0$, one has $0\le r_-<r_+$ and $r_-=0$ exactly when $a=0$. Thus $\Delta=(r-r_+)(r-r_-)>0$ for $r>r_+$. Also $\Sigma\ge r^2>0$, $A:=r^2+a^2>0$, and $q=\gamma(\xi,\xi)\ge0$. The global formula in [F1] is a smooth symmetric tensor because its sphere tensors and scalar functions are smooth, its denominators are nonzero, and its finite sums and products are smooth by [F6]. The stated formula for $N$ is smooth: repeated use of [F5] makes $x\mapsto x^{-1}$ smooth on $(0,\infty)$, [F6] composes this with $\Sigma\Delta$, and $T,\Phi$ are smooth by [F1]; hence $N$ is a smooth vector field in the sense of [F7].

On a polar chart put $q=\sin^2\theta$. The one-forms $e^0=\sqrt{\Delta/\Sigma}(dt-aq\,d\phi)$, $e^1=\sqrt{\Sigma/\Delta}\,dr$, $e^2=\sqrt{\Sigma}\,d\theta$, and $e^3=\sin\theta\,\Sigma^{-1/2}(A\,d\phi-a\,dt)$ are smooth: repeated application of [F5] gives every derivative of the positive powers $x^{1/2}$ and $x^{-1/2}$ on $(0,\infty)$, and [F6] gives smoothness after composition with the positive smooth functions $\Delta,\Sigma$. The determinant of the coefficient matrix of $(e^0,e^3)$ relative to $(dt,d\phi)$ is $\sqrt{\Delta}\sin\theta$, which is nonzero when $0<\theta<\pi$. Expanding the global formula of [F1] gives $g=-(e^0)^2+(e^1)^2+(e^2)^2+(e^3)^2$; hence $g$ has signature $(-,+,+,+)$ at every point off the axis.

At either axis point $\xi^\flat=0$, $\Sigma=A$, and the global expression in [F1] restricts to $g=-(\Delta/A)\,dt^2+(A/\Delta)\,dr^2+A\gamma$ on the tangent directions there. The first coefficient is negative and the radial and sphere terms are positive because $A,\Delta>0$ and $\gamma$ is positive definite. Thus $g$ is nondegenerate with the same signature at the axes. The global definition in [F1] already gives smoothness there, so this proves the asserted signature on all of $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}$.

On a polar chart put $q=\sin^2\theta$. Direct inversion of the $t,\phi$ block gives $\Sigma\Delta\,g^{tt}=-(A^2-a^2\Delta q)$ and $\Sigma\Delta\,g^{t\phi}=-2aMr$. Here $0<\Delta<A$ and $0\le q\le1$, so $A^2-a^2\Delta q\ge A^2-a^2\Delta\ge A^2-a^2A=Ar^2>0$. The second inequality uses $\Delta<A$ and $a^2\ge0$; equality is allowed when $a=0$. Hence $g^{-1}(dt,dt)=g^{tt}<0$. The same inverse components show $-\sharp_g(dt)=\frac{A^2-a^2\Delta q}{\Sigma\Delta}T+\frac{2aMr}{\Sigma\Delta}\Phi=N$ on this chart. At an axis point smoothness of the inverse from [F3] and step 2.2 give $g^{-1}(dt,dt)=-A/\Delta<0$; the smooth global fields $N$ and $-\sharp_g(dt)$ agree on the dense polar chart, hence agree on the axes as well. Thus $g(N,N)=g^{-1}(dt,dt)<0$ everywhere, and [F4] makes $N$ a time orientation.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). The cotangent space $T_p^*M$ is
the algebraic dual of $T_pM$ ([[def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional]]).

**Musical isomorphisms.** Define the **flat map**

$$\flat_p:T_pM\longrightarrow T_p^*M,\qquad \flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot),$$

so that $\flat_p(v)(w)=g_p(v,w)$; it is $\mathbb R$-linear by bilinearity of
$g_p$. Its kernel is $\{v:g_p(v,w)=0\text{ for all }w\}=\{0\}$ because $g_p$ is
nondegenerate, and $\dim_{\mathbb R}T_pM=\dim_{\mathbb R}T_p^*M=4$ since the
coordinate derivations of a chart form a basis of $T_pM$
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]); hence
$\flat_p$ is a linear isomorphism and has an inverse
$\sharp_p:T_p^*M\to T_pM$.

**Inverse metric.** The **inverse metric** at $p$ is the symmetric bilinear form

$$g_p^{-1}:T_p^*M\times T_p^*M\longrightarrow\mathbb R,\qquad g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta).$$

It is symmetric because $g_p$ is, and it is nondegenerate: if
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta)=0$ for all $\beta$, then $g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\cdot)=0$,
so $\sharp_p\alpha=0$ and hence $\alpha=0$.

**Components in a chart.** Let $(U,x)$ be a smooth chart and
$g_{ab}(q)=g_q(\partial_a|_q,\partial_b|_q)$ the components of $g$; let
$dx^a|_q$ be the differential of the coordinate function $x^a$ at $q$
([[def-differential-of-a-smooth-map]]), so that
$dx^a|_q(\partial_b|_q)=\partial_b|_q(x^a)=\delta^a{}_b$. Define the components
of the inverse metric in this chart by

$$g^{ab}(q):=g_q^{-1}\bigl(dx^a|_q,\,dx^b|_q\bigr),\qquad q\in U,$$

so that $\sharp_q(dx^a|_q)=\sum_bg^{ab}(q)\,\partial_b|_q$; equivalently
$(g^{ab}(q))$ is the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab}(q))$ at every $q$, that is

$$g^{ac}(q)\,g_{cb}(q)=\delta^a{}_b,\qquad g_{ac}(q)g^{cb}(q)=\delta_a{}^b,$$

because $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=dx^a|_q(\partial_c|_q)=\delta^a{}_c$
and also $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=\sum_bg^{ab}(q)g_{bc}(q)$. In
particular $g^{ab}=g^{ba}$. The components $g^{ab}$ depend smoothly on $q$;
this is proved in [[lem-gr-inverse-metric-is-smooth]].

**Raising, lowering and metric trace.** Let $A$ be a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field on an open set $V\subseteq M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). At each $p\in V$ define the
endomorphism

$$A^\sharp_p:T_pM\to T_pM,\qquad A^\sharp_p(v):=\sharp_p\bigl(A_p(v,\cdot)\bigr),$$

characterized by $g_p(A^\sharp_p(v),w)=A_p(v,w)$ for all $w\in T_pM$; it is
self-adjoint for $g_p$ because $A_p$ is symmetric. Its **metric trace** is

$$\operatorname{tr}_g(A)(p):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(A^\sharp_p\bigr)$$

with the trace of an endomorphism as in [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. In a
chart the raised, mixed and doubly raised components are

$$A^{ab}:=g^{ac}g^{bd}A_{cd},\qquad A^a{}_b:=g^{ac}A_{cb},\qquad\text{and}\qquad \operatorname{tr}_g(A)=g^{ab}A_{ab},$$

the last identity obtained by evaluating in a $g_p$-orthonormal basis
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$, where $g_p(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ by
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]] so that
$g^{ab}A_{ab}=\sum_a g^{aa}A_{aa}=-A(e_0,e_0)+A(e_1,e_1)+A(e_2,e_2)+A(e_3,e_3)$,
which is the trace of the endomorphism $v\mapsto\sharp_p(A_p(v,\cdot))$ in that
basis. All these operations are pointwise and depend only on $g$, $A$ and the
duality pairing, not on a chart.

**Conventions.** Raising and lowering apply to one index at a time and preserve
index order; $A_{ab}$, $A^a{}_b$ and $A^{ab}$ denote the same tensor $A$ with
indices positioned by $g$. The musical isomorphisms and the inverse metric are
defined for every smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of this library; no choice
principle is used in this definition, every ingredient being pointwise linear
algebra over $\mathbb R$ together with the pointwise nondegeneracy of $g_p$.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$g_p^{-1}$ and $g^{ab}$ be the inverse metric and its chart components as in
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]. Then:

1. For every smooth chart $(U,x)$ the component functions $g^{ab}:U\to\mathbb R$
   are $C^\infty$ on $U$.
2. For overlapping smooth charts $(U,x)$, $(V,y)$ the components satisfy the
   contravariant transformation law

$$g'^{ab}(u)=\sum_{c,d=0}^{3}\frac{\partial y^a}{\partial x^c}\bigl(x(u)\bigr)\, \frac{\partial y^b}{\partial x^d}\bigl(x(u)\bigr)\,g^{cd}\bigl(x(u)\bigr),\qquad u\in y(U\cap V),$$

where every component evaluated at a coordinate tuple is its coordinate
representative, as in [[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]],
$x(u)$ denotes $(x\circ y^{-1})(u)$, and $\partial y^a/\partial x^c$ are
the entries of $D(y\circ x^{-1})$.

3. Consequently the pointwise bilinear forms $g_p^{-1}$ on $T_p^*M$ are
   presented by component functions that are smooth in every chart and glue by
   the contravariant law; the inverse metric is a well-defined smooth component
   family determined by $g$ alone.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary, so that $M$ is Hausdorff
and second countable and carries a maximal smooth atlas
([[def-smooth-manifold]]). Let $g$ be a smooth covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$
in the sense of [[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]. Then $g$ assigns
to every $p\in M$ a bilinear form $g_p:T_pM\times T_pM\to\mathbb R$
([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]).

**(a) Lorentzian metric.** The field $g$ is a **Lorentzian metric of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$** on $M$ when it is symmetric and nondegenerate, and at every
$p\in M$ the pair $(T_pM,g_p)$ is a Lorentz vector space of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ in the sense of [[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]: that is, $g_p$ has
inertia $(3,1,0)$, so that some — equivalently every — basis of $T_pM$ in which
the matrix of $g_p$ is diagonal has exactly one negative and three positive
diagonal entries. The pair $(M,g)$ is a **smooth Lorentzian four-manifold** (or
Lorentzian manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$). In a smooth chart $(U,x)$ the
**components** of $g$ are the $C^\infty$ functions
$g_{ab}(q)=g_q(\partial_a|_q,\partial_b|_q)$ of
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]], and $g_{ab}=g_{ba}$ by symmetry.
We use indices $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$ and the Einstein summation convention, with
components in a chart written as lower-case indexed symbols and equations
between indexed fields understood basis-independently. These conventions are
fixed once for this library and the physical reading of the symbols is recorded
with the framework postulates, separately from this mathematical definition.

**(b) Pointwise causal structure.** For every $p\in M$ the vocabulary of
[[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] applies to the Lorentz vector
space $(T_pM,g_p)$: a tangent vector $v\in T_pM$ is **timelike** when
$g_p(v,v)<0$, **null** when $v\neq0$ and $g_p(v,v)=0$, **spacelike** when
$g_p(v,v)>0$, and **causal** when it is timelike or null. Every nonzero
$v\in T_pM$ has exactly one causal character. The **timelike set**
$T_p:=\{v\in T_pM:g_p(v,v)<0\}$ has exactly two connected components, each
nonempty, open, convex and path-connected; each $g_p$-orthonormal basis
$e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3$ of $T_pM$ satisfies $g_p(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$
for some ordering, so in particular nonzero orthonormal vectors exist at every
point ([[lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis]],
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]]).

**(c) Time orientation.** A **time orientation** of $(M,g)$, also called a
**choice of future cone**, is a smooth vector field $N$ on $M$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]], whose tangent-bundle
smooth structure uses the axiom $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of
[[def-countable-choice]]; this is the only use of that axiom in this
definition) such that

$$g_p(N_p,N_p)<0\qquad\text{for every }p\in M .$$

The function $p\mapsto g_p(N_p,N_p)$ is $C^\infty$ because $g$ is a smooth
covariant $2$-tensor field and $N$ a smooth field, so the condition is a
pointwise strict inequality between a smooth function and $0$; since
$g_p(N_p,N_p)<0$ implies $N_p\neq0$, a time orientation is nowhere vanishing.
A **time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold** is a triple $(M,g,N)$
consisting of a smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and a time orientation $N$.

Given a time orientation $N$ and $p\in M$, the vector $N_p$ is timelike, and we
**define** a nonzero causal vector $v\in T_pM$ to be **future-directed** when
$g_p(v,N_p)<0$ and **past-directed** when $g_p(v,N_p)>0$. The classification of
nonzero causal vectors into exactly these two classes, and its agreement with
the two components of the timelike set (the future component is the component
$C_p^+$ containing $N_p$, and the future causal vectors form
$\operatorname{cl}(C_p^+)\setminus\{0\}$), is proved in
[[lem-gr-future-causal-classification-by-a-timelike-field]]; in particular no

mutually exclusive. Replacing $N$ by $-N$ reverses every future/past label, and

these quantities in the physical conventions, fix a positive real scaling
parameter $c$ (with no physical meaning or dimension in this mathematical

from a nonempty open real interval $I$ ([[def-interval]],

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, so that $TM$ carries its canonical smooth
structure. Let $M$ be a smooth manifold. A **smooth vector field** on $M$ is a
smooth section

$$ X:M\to TM $$

of the tangent-bundle projection $\pi:TM\to M$. Thus $\pi\circ X=\operatorname{id}_M$.

Equivalently, for each $p\in M$ the value $X(p)$ is a tangent vector in $T_pM$,
and the dependence on $p$ is smooth with respect to the canonical smooth
structure on $TM$.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

citations.quote:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the tangent-bundle smooth structure of the
Lorentzian conventions.

Let $(\mathcal M,g,N)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold with
its metric-selected connection $\nabla$. A smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field $K_{ab}$ is a **rank-two Killing tensor** when

$$\nabla_{(a}K_{bc)}:=\frac13\left(\nabla_aK_{bc}+\nabla_bK_{ca}+\nabla_cK_{ab}\right)=0.$$

For a smooth curve $\gamma:I\to\mathcal M$ with open interval domain and affine
parameter $\lambda$, write $v=\dot\gamma$. If $\nabla_vv=0$, the curve is an
affinely parametrized geodesic, and $K_{ab}v^av^b$ is its associated quadratic
geodesic integral. It is called **reducible** if it is a finite constant
linear combination of $g_{ab}$ and symmetric products
$\xi^\flat\odot\eta^\flat$, where $\xi,\eta$ are Killing fields,
$\xi^\flat:=g(\xi,\cdot)$, and
$\alpha\odot\beta:=(\alpha\otimes\beta+\beta\otimes\alpha)/2$.

Let $M$ be a smooth manifold without boundary with affine connection $\nabla$, and let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with nonempty interior. A smooth curve $\gamma:I\to M$ is an **affinely parametrized geodesic** when
$$D_t\gamma'(t)=0\qquad(t\in I),$$
with one-sided interpretation at an included endpoint. Constant curves are geodesics. Unless another parametrization is explicitly stated, “geodesic” means affinely parametrized geodesic.

For a given connection on $E$ and a smooth curve on an interval with nonempty interior, the **covariant derivative along the curve** is
$$D_tV=(\gamma^*\nabla)_{\partial/\partial t}V.$$
Here $V$ is a section of the pullback bundle as in [[def-vector-field-and-section-along-a-smooth-curve]], and the pullback connection exists by [[thm-pullback-connection-is-well-defined-and-functorial]]. It is real-linear and satisfies $D_t(fV)=f'V+fD_tV$ for functions of the parameter.

At an included endpoint the smooth up-to-boundary coefficients have their one-sided derivative; equivalently any smooth local extension of the coefficients gives this value, because extensions agreeing on a one-sided interval have the same derivative there. For a piecewise smooth curve the derivative is defined on each piece, with separate one-sided derivatives at corners; those derivatives are not required to agree. A singleton interval carries no derivative operator under this convention and will have identity transport by definition. A zero section or a rank-zero bundle gives zero covariant derivative. Constant base curves can have sections with nonzero coefficient derivative.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Assume
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).
For this general metric define $\flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot)$,
$\sharp_p:=\flat_p^{-1}$, and
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta)$.
Nondegeneracy makes $\flat_p$ injective and hence invertible between the
four-dimensional tangent space and its dual. In a chart, $g^{ab}$ are the
entries of the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$. These definitions agree with
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] in its Lorentzian scope.
Here and below repeated upper/lower indices are summed over $0,1,2,3$.
This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth local vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth local }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$, meaning torsion-free and satisfying
$Xg(Y,Z)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$ for smooth local fields
(the conditions of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] extended here to
nondegenerate $g$); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components defined above
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on
$T^r_sM:=(TM)^{\otimes r}\otimes(T^*M)^{\otimes s}$, for integers $r,s\ge0$,
constructed by [[lem-finite-tensor-products-of-smooth-vector-bundles]]. A
type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$ is a multilinear map
$(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\to\mathbb R$
([[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]); a smooth
tensor field is a section with smooth coefficients in each local product

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the tangent-bundle smooth structure of the
Lorentzian conventions.

Let $(\mathcal M,g,N)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold with
its metric-selected connection $\nabla$. A smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field $K_{ab}$ is a **rank-two Killing tensor** when

$$\nabla_{(a}K_{bc)}:=\frac13\left(\nabla_aK_{bc}+\nabla_bK_{ca}+\nabla_cK_{ab}\right)=0.$$

For a smooth curve $\gamma:I\to\mathcal M$ with open interval domain and affine
parameter $\lambda$, write $v=\dot\gamma$. If $\nabla_vv=0$, the curve is an
affinely parametrized geodesic, and $K_{ab}v^av^b$ is its associated quadratic
geodesic integral. It is called **reducible** if it is a finite constant
linear combination of $g_{ab}$ and symmetric products
$\xi^\flat\odot\eta^\flat$, where $\xi,\eta$ are Killing fields,
$\xi^\flat:=g(\xi,\cdot)$, and
$\alpha\odot\beta:=(\alpha\otimes\beta+\beta\otimes\alpha)/2$.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
For a given connection on $E$ and a smooth curve on an interval with nonempty interior, the **covariant derivative along the curve** is
$$D_tV=(\gamma^*\nabla)_{\partial/\partial t}V.$$
Here $V$ is a section of the pullback bundle as in [[def-vector-field-and-section-along-a-smooth-curve]], and the pullback connection exists by [[thm-pullback-connection-is-well-defined-and-functorial]]. It is real-linear and satisfies $D_t(fV)=f'V+fD_tV$ for functions of the parameter.

At an included endpoint the smooth up-to-boundary coefficients have their one-sided derivative; equivalently any smooth local extension of the coefficients gives this value, because extensions agreeing on a one-sided interval have the same derivative there. For a piecewise smooth curve the derivative is defined on each piece, with separate one-sided derivatives at corners; those derivatives are not required to agree. A singleton interval carries no derivative operator under this convention and will have identity transport by definition. A zero section or a rank-zero bundle gives zero covariant derivative. Constant base curves can have sections with nonzero coefficient derivative.

with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],

citations.quote:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the tangent-bundle smooth structure of the
Lorentzian conventions.

Let $M>0$ and $a\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $|a|<M$, and put
$r_\pm:=M\pm\sqrt{M^2-a^2}$.

Let $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}:=\mathbb R\times(r_+,\infty)\times S^2$ carry the
product smooth structure, where $S^2=\{(x,y,z)\in\mathbb R^3:x^2+y^2+z^2=1\}$
has its usual smooth structure and round metric $\gamma_{S^2}$. Let
$\pi:\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}\to S^2$ be the third projection, let $\xi$ be the
smooth rotation field on $S^2$ generated by $(x,y,z)\mapsto(-y,x,0)$, and put
$\gamma:=\pi^*\gamma_{S^2}$ and
$\xi^\flat:=\pi^*(\gamma_{S^2}(\xi,\cdot))$. Let $t,r$ be the first and
second coordinate functions on $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}$, and let
$\zeta:=z\circ\pi$ be the third Euclidean coordinate on the sphere factor.
Define the global smooth functions

$$\Sigma:=r^2+a^2\zeta^2,\qquad \Delta:=r^2-2Mr+a^2.$$

On a polar chart $0<\theta<\pi$, $\phi\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$, one has
$\zeta=\cos\theta$, $\Sigma=r^2+a^2\cos^2\theta$,
$\gamma=d\theta^2+\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2$, and
$\xi^\flat=\sin^2\theta\,d\phi$.

Define the symmetric covariant $2$-tensor $g$ globally on $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}$
by

$$g=-\left(1-\frac{2Mr}{\Sigma}\right)dt\otimes dt+\frac{\Sigma}{\Delta}\,dr\otimes dr+\Sigma\gamma+\frac{a^2(\Sigma+2Mr)}{\Sigma}\,\xi^\flat\otimes\xi^\flat-\frac{2aMr}{\Sigma}\left(dt\otimes\xi^\flat+\xi^\flat\otimes dt\right).$$

Its Boyer-Lindquist line element on the polar chart is

$$ds^2=-\left(1-\frac{2Mr}{\Sigma}\right)dt^2-\frac{4Mar\sin^2\theta}{\Sigma}\,dt\,d\phi+\frac{\Sigma}{\Delta}\,dr^2+\Sigma\,d\theta^2+\frac{(r^2+a^2)^2-a^2\Delta\sin^2\theta}{\Sigma}\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2.$$

The displayed cross term is $2g_{t\phi}\,dt\,d\phi$. This definition makes
no nondegeneracy or signature claim; Lorentzian signature and a time orientation
are established separately.

For $M>0$, $|a|<M$, and the Kerr exterior tensor datum, define
$T:=\partial_t$, $\Phi:=\xi$, $A:=r^2+a^2$, and $q:=\gamma(\xi,\xi)$.
The global vector field
$$N:=\frac{A^2-a^2\Delta q}{\Sigma\Delta}\,T+\frac{2aMr}{\Sigma\Delta}\,\Phi$$
is smooth; the tensor $g$ is smooth, symmetric, nondegenerate, and has
signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on all of
$\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}=\mathbb R\times(r_+,\infty)\times S^2$; and
$N=-\sharp_g(dt)$ is timelike. Thus $N$ defines a time orientation of this
Lorentzian four-manifold.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $\xi$ be a smooth vector field
on $M$ ([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]). The **Lie
derivative of the metric along $\xi$**, written $\mathcal L_\xi g$, is the
smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field obtained by the flow definition of
[[def-lie-derivative-of-a-tensor-field]] applied to $g$: for the local flow
$\Phi_t$ of $\xi$,

$$\mathcal L_\xi g:=\frac{d}{dt}\Big|_{t=0}\Phi_t^*g .$$

The field $\xi$ is a **Killing field** of $(M,g)$ (an **isometry generator**,
or a **Killing vector**) when

$$\mathcal L_\xi g=0 .$$

The equivalent local characterization

$$\mathcal L_\xi g=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\nabla_a\xi_b+\nabla_b\xi_a=0,$$

where $\nabla$ is the metric-selected connection of $g$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and
$\xi_b:=g_{bc}\xi^c$ is the lowered field, is proved in
[[thm-gr-killing-and-on-shell-matter-identities]] clause (a); the definition
itself asserts neither direction. Whether a given metric has Killing fields is
a property of that metric: neither existence nor uniqueness of a Killing field
is asserted here, and a general metric has none beyond the trivial field
$\xi=0$.

For a covariant $k$-tensor $T=T_{i_1\cdots i_k}dx^{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes dx^{i_k}$, $$ (\mathcal L_XT)_{i_1\cdots i_k}=X^j\partial_jT_{i_1\cdots i_k}+\sum_a(\partial_{i_a}X^j)T_{i_1\cdots j\cdots i_k}. $$

Assume Countable Choice for the smooth tangent-bundle and time-orientation conventions of the Lorentzian suppliers. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$. A **closed spacelike two-surface** is a nonempty smooth embedded two-manifold $S\subset M$ that is compact without boundary. Let $\iota:S\hookrightarrow M$ be the inclusion and let its induced metric be $q:=\iota^*g$; require $q$ to be positive definite. Its normal bundle is $\mathcal NS=(TS)^\perp$. Work on an open set $U\subseteq S$ carrying a smooth ordered pair of future null normal fields $\ell,k$ with $g(\ell,\ell)=g(k,k)=0$ and $g(\ell,k)=-2$; such pairs exist locally by the preceding lemma. No global pair is part of the definition unless one is explicitly supplied.

For tangent fields $X,Y$ on $U$, define the null second fundamental form, expansion and shear by
$$\chi_\ell(X,Y):=g(\nabla_X\ell,Y),\qquad \theta_\ell:=\operatorname{tr}_q\chi_\ell,\qquad \sigma_\ell:=\chi_\ell-\frac{\theta_\ell}{2}q.$$
Here $\nabla$ is the metric-selected connection; its derivative of a section along $S$ means the pullback connection, equivalently the derivative of any smooth ambient extension along tangent directions. The preceding lemma establishes extension independence, symmetry of $\chi_\ell$, and positive definiteness of the screen metric. A **normal-frame boost** is the change $\ell\mapsto e^f\ell$, $k\mapsto e^{-f}k$ for a smooth real function $f$ on $U$. It leaves $q$ fixed; $\chi_\ell,\theta_\ell,\sigma_\ell$ scale by $e^f$.

A **null geodesic hypersurface congruence from $U$** along the chosen initial normal field $\ell$ is a smooth map $F:U\times J\to M$, where $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ is a nonempty open interval containing $0$, such that $F(p,0)=p$ and $\partial_\lambda F(p,0)=\ell_p$ for every $p\in U$, each curve $\gamma_p(\lambda):=F(p,\lambda)$ is future-directed and null, and its tangent $\ell:=\partial_\lambda F$ obeys the affine geodesic equation
$$D_\lambda\ell=0$$
along every curve $\gamma_p$; here $D_\lambda$ is the covariant derivative along a curve from [[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]. For each $p\in U$, let $J_{\mathrm{reg}}(p)$ be the connected component containing $0$ of the parameter values for which $d(F_\lambda)_p:T_pU\to T_{F(p,\lambda)}M$ is injective and the pullback form $(X,Y)\mapsto g(d(F_\lambda)_pX,d(F_\lambda)_pY)$ is positive definite on $T_pU$. Require, for every $\lambda\in J$, that its variation directions satisfy
$$g_{F(p,\lambda)}\bigl(\ell(p,\lambda),dF_{(p,\lambda)}(X,0)\bigr)=0\qquad(X\in T_pU).$$
Thus its variation directions are orthogonal to $\ell$. For $\lambda\in J_{\mathrm{reg}}(p)$, the map $F$ has rank three locally near $(p,\lambda)$: its two section directions are spacelike and orthogonal to the nonzero null vector $\ell$. Its local image is a null hypersurface, with tangent space $\ell^\perp$ and induced radical $\mathbb R\ell$, as in [[lem-gr-fx-null-normal-plane-and-screen]]. The parameter $\lambda$ is affine. On each section in $J_{\mathrm{reg}}$, the **screen** is $\mathscr S=\ell^\perp/\mathbb R\ell$ with metric $\bar q([X],[Y])=g(X,Y)$; it is the positive two-dimensional quotient, identified isometrically with the tangent plane of that section by projection. The induced form on the full null hypersurface has radical $\mathbb R\ell$ and has no inverse. All traces and inverses in this definition are taken on the screen.

All screen bundles associated with this congruence are understood as bundles over the parameter domain $U\times J$: the notation $\mathscr S_{F(p,\lambda)}$ denotes the branch determined by $(p,\lambda)$, so self-intersections do not identify distinct screen fibers. For each $\lambda\in J$, the screen Jacobi map $A_\lambda:T_pS\to\mathscr S_{F(p,\lambda)}$ sends $X$ to the screen class of the variation field $J_X(\lambda):=dF_{(p,\lambda)}(X,0)$; it is invertible for $\lambda\in J_{\mathrm{reg}}(p)$. A **focal instant** is a positive parameter in $J$ where $A_\lambda$ loses rank; the **first focal instant**, if it exists, is the least such parameter after $0$. Along an affine generator the screen derivative is $\mathcal D_\ell[X]:=[D_\ell X]$; it is independent of the representative, by the preceding lemma. On $J_{\mathrm{reg}}$, the derivative $A_\lambda'$ is taken using $\mathcal D_\ell$, and the **optical endomorphism** is $B_\lambda:=A_\lambda'A_\lambda^{-1}$. Its **optical expansion** is $\theta:=\operatorname{tr}B$, and its **optical shear** is $\sigma:=B-\frac12\theta\,\mathrm{id}_{\mathscr S}$. Since the congruence is normal to a null hypersurface, $B$ is self-adjoint. Its antisymmetric part $\omega:=(B-B^*)/2$, called the twist, therefore vanishes. At $\lambda=0$, $B$ is the endomorphism $q^{-1}\chi_\ell$ and these optical quantities agree with $\theta_\ell,\sigma_\ell$.

No orientation of $M$, $S$, or the screen is required for these constructions. Indeed, if two orthonormal screen frames are related by a real $2\times2$ matrix $O$ with $O^{\mathsf T}O=I_2$, then the endomorphism matrices obey $\widehat B=O^{-1}BO$ and $\widehat\sigma=O^{-1}\sigma O$. Cyclicity of the matrix trace gives $\operatorname{tr}\widehat B=\operatorname{tr}B$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\widehat\sigma^2)=\operatorname{tr}(\sigma^2)=|\sigma|_{\bar q}^2$; the last equality follows by summing the squared entries of the symmetric shear matrix in an orthonormal frame. This includes $\det O=-1$. The screen inner products and the rank of $A_\lambda$ are likewise invariant under changes of frame, so neither the index-form contractions nor the focal condition uses a signed screen area form. The preceding lemma constructs normal pairs using the supplied time orientation and only a local spacelike complement; changing the complement's sign interchanges the two future null rays. No global ordered pair follows. If an orientation is additionally supplied, the same formulas apply on that oriented subclass.

Let $I \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be order-convex with at least two elements
([[def-interval]]) and let $f : I \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $I$
([[def-continuity-real]]). Call $G : I \to \mathbb{R}$ a **primitive of $f$ on
$I$** when $G$ is differentiable at every point of $I$ as a function on $I$ with
$G' = f$ there ([[def-derivative]]). Then:

1. **Existence.** Fix $c_0 \in I$. The function
   $$F : I \to \mathbb{R}, \qquad F(x) \;:=\; \int_{c_0}^x f$$
   is defined at every $x \in I$ ([[def-oriented-integral]],
   [[def-the-integral-function]]) and is a primitive of $f$ on $I$.
2. **Uniqueness up to a constant.** If $G_1$ and $G_2$ are primitives of $f$ on
   $I$ then there is a real $k$ with $G_1(x) = G_2(x) + k$ for every $x \in I$.
3. **Evaluation.** If $a, b \in I$ with $a < b$ and $G$ is any primitive of $f$
   on $I$, then
   $$\int_a^b f \;=\; G(b) - G(a) .$$

**The scope is exactly the continuous case, and that is not a limitation of the
proof.** An integrable function need not have a primitive, and a function with a
primitive need not be integrable; this corollary is precisely the intersection
where both fundamental theorems apply, and both witnesses are on the companion
page.

For $a>0$, the function $x\mapsto a^x$ is continuous on $\mathbb R$ and
$$(a^x)'=a^x\log a.$$
For $\alpha\in\mathbb R$, the function $x\mapsto x^\alpha$ is continuous and differentiable on $(0,\infty)$, with
$$(x^\alpha)'=\alpha x^{\alpha-1}.$$

Let $k\in\mathbb N$. Finite componentwise sums and products of $C^k$ Euclidean maps are $C^k$, and a composite of composable $C^k$ Euclidean maps is $C^k$. Scalar multiples are included among the finite componentwise operations. The assertions remain valid on an empty open domain.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). The cotangent space $T_p^*M$ is
the algebraic dual of $T_pM$ ([[def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional]]).

**Musical isomorphisms.** Define the **flat map**

$$\flat_p:T_pM\longrightarrow T_p^*M,\qquad \flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot),$$

so that $\flat_p(v)(w)=g_p(v,w)$; it is $\mathbb R$-linear by bilinearity of
$g_p$. Its kernel is $\{v:g_p(v,w)=0\text{ for all }w\}=\{0\}$ because $g_p$ is
nondegenerate, and $\dim_{\mathbb R}T_pM=\dim_{\mathbb R}T_p^*M=4$ since the
coordinate derivations of a chart form a basis of $T_pM$
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]); hence
$\flat_p$ is a linear isomorphism and has an inverse
$\sharp_p:T_p^*M\to T_pM$.

**Inverse metric.** The **inverse metric** at $p$ is the symmetric bilinear form

$$g_p^{-1}:T_p^*M\times T_p^*M\longrightarrow\mathbb R,\qquad g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta).$$

It is symmetric because $g_p$ is, and it is nondegenerate: if
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta)=0$ for all $\beta$, then $g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\cdot)=0$,
so $\sharp_p\alpha=0$ and hence $\alpha=0$.

**Components in a chart.** Let $(U,x)$ be a smooth chart and
$g_{ab}(q)=g_q(\partial_a|_q,\partial_b|_q)$ the components of $g$; let
$dx^a|_q$ be the differential of the coordinate function $x^a$ at $q$
([[def-differential-of-a-smooth-map]]), so that
$dx^a|_q(\partial_b|_q)=\partial_b|_q(x^a)=\delta^a{}_b$. Define the components
of the inverse metric in this chart by

$$g^{ab}(q):=g_q^{-1}\bigl(dx^a|_q,\,dx^b|_q\bigr),\qquad q\in U,$$

so that $\sharp_q(dx^a|_q)=\sum_bg^{ab}(q)\,\partial_b|_q$; equivalently
$(g^{ab}(q))$ is the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab}(q))$ at every $q$, that is

$$g^{ac}(q)\,g_{cb}(q)=\delta^a{}_b,\qquad g_{ac}(q)g^{cb}(q)=\delta_a{}^b,$$

because $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=dx^a|_q(\partial_c|_q)=\delta^a{}_c$
and also $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=\sum_bg^{ab}(q)g_{bc}(q)$. In
particular $g^{ab}=g^{ba}$. The components $g^{ab}$ depend smoothly on $q$;
this is proved in [[lem-gr-inverse-metric-is-smooth]].

**Raising, lowering and metric trace.** Let $A$ be a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field on an open set $V\subseteq M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). At each $p\in V$ define the
endomorphism

$$A^\sharp_p:T_pM\to T_pM,\qquad A^\sharp_p(v):=\sharp_p\bigl(A_p(v,\cdot)\bigr),$$

characterized by $g_p(A^\sharp_p(v),w)=A_p(v,w)$ for all $w\in T_pM$; it is
self-adjoint for $g_p$ because $A_p$ is symmetric. Its **metric trace** is

$$\operatorname{tr}_g(A)(p):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(A^\sharp_p\bigr)$$

with the trace of an endomorphism as in [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. In a
chart the raised, mixed and doubly raised components are

$$A^{ab}:=g^{ac}g^{bd}A_{cd},\qquad A^a{}_b:=g^{ac}A_{cb},\qquad\text{and}\qquad \operatorname{tr}_g(A)=g^{ab}A_{ab},$$

the last identity obtained by evaluating in a $g_p$-orthonormal basis
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$, where $g_p(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ by
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]] so that
$g^{ab}A_{ab}=\sum_a g^{aa}A_{aa}=-A(e_0,e_0)+A(e_1,e_1)+A(e_2,e_2)+A(e_3,e_3)$,
which is the trace of the endomorphism $v\mapsto\sharp_p(A_p(v,\cdot))$ in that
basis. All these operations are pointwise and depend only on $g$, $A$ and the
duality pairing, not on a chart.

**Conventions.** Raising and lowering apply to one index at a time and preserve
index order; $A_{ab}$, $A^a{}_b$ and $A^{ab}$ denote the same tensor $A$ with
indices positioned by $g$. The musical isomorphisms and the inverse metric are
defined for every smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of this library; no choice
principle is used in this definition, every ingredient being pointwise linear
algebra over $\mathbb R$ together with the pointwise nondegeneracy of $g_p$.

The functions $\sin$ and $\cos$ are differentiable on $\mathbb R$, with
$$(\sin x)'=\cos x,\qquad(\cos x)'=-\sin x.$$
Also $\sin0=0$ and $\cos0=1$.

statement.

> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

derivations.claim: The coefficients in [F1] have no $t$ or $\phi$ dependence. For $T=\partial_t$ and $\Phi=\partial_\phi$, the coordinate components are constant, so every term in [F4] vanishes; hence $\mathcal L_Tg=\mathcal L_\Phi g=0$ and both fields are Killing by [F3].

Choose $0<\varepsilon<r_+/2$ and use the extension manifold $\overline{\mathcal M}:=\mathbb R_v\times(r_+-\varepsilon,\infty)\times S^2$ with its product smooth structure. Let $\bar\pi:\overline{\mathcal M}\to S^2$ be the sphere projection, $\bar\gamma:=\bar\pi^*\gamma_{S^2}$, $\eta:=\bar\pi^*(\gamma_{S^2}(\xi,\cdot))$, and $q:=\bar\gamma(\xi,\xi)=|\xi|_{\bar\gamma}^2$. These are global smooth tensors or functions; on a polar chart of the new sphere factor, $\eta=\sin^2\theta\,d\widetilde\phi$ and $q=\sin^2\theta$. Fix $r_0>r_+$ and define $f(r)=\int_{r_0}^r (s^2+a^2)/\Delta(s)\,ds$ and $h(r)=\int_{r_0}^r a/\Delta(s)\,ds$ on $(r_+,\infty)$. Their integrands are smooth because $\Delta>0$: repeated use of [F7] gives all derivatives of $\Delta^{-1}$, and [F8] handles the polynomial products. [F6] gives $f,h\in C^1$, and successive differentiation of $f'=(r^2+a^2)/\Delta$ and $h'=a/\Delta$ shows that both primitives are smooth. Set $v=t+f(r)$ and, on the sphere factor, replace each point $(x,y,z)$ by $R_{h(r)}(x,y,z):=(x\cos h-y\sin h,x\sin h+y\cos h,z)$. Repeated application of [F10] makes this rotation smoothly dependent on $r$, and its inverse is $R_{-h(r)}$. Thus the exterior map is a smooth diffeomorphism, with coordinate Jacobian determinant $1$ on every polar chart; there $\widetilde\phi=\phi+h(r)$ and the pullback of the original $\xi^\flat$ is $\eta-aq\Delta^{-1}dr$. Substitution in [F1], using $\Sigma^2+a^2q(\Sigma+2Mr)=(r^2+a^2)^2-a^2\Delta q$, gives the global ingoing expression
$$g=-\frac{\Delta-a^2q}{\Sigma}\,dv\otimes dv+dv\otimes dr+dr\otimes dv+\Sigma\bar\gamma+\frac{a^2(\Sigma+2Mr)}{\Sigma}\eta\otimes\eta-\frac{2aMr}{\Sigma}(dv\otimes\eta+\eta\otimes dv)-a(dr\otimes\eta+\eta\otimes dr).$$
For every $r>r_+-\varepsilon>r_+/2>0$, one has $\Sigma>0$ and $\Delta=A-2Mr<A$, where $A:=r^2+a^2$. If $\Delta\ge0$, then $A^2-a^2\Delta q\ge A^2-a^2\Delta\ge A^2-a^2A=Ar^2>0$; if $\Delta<0$, then $A^2-a^2\Delta q\ge A^2>0$. Consequently the angular restriction in an off-axis polar chart, $\Sigma\,d\theta^2+\frac{q(A^2-a^2\Delta q)}{\Sigma}\,d\widetilde\phi^2$, is positive definite. The determinant of the full metric matrix there is $-\Sigma^2q<0$; its Schur complement in the $(v,r)$ directions is symmetric with negative determinant, hence has one negative and one positive eigenvalue. The full metric therefore has signature $(-,+,+,+)$ off the axis. At an axis point $\eta=0$ and $\Sigma=A$; the $(v,r)$ block has matrix $\begin{pmatrix}-\Delta/\Sigma&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ of determinant $-1$, and the sphere block is $\Sigma\gamma_{S^2}$ on the tangent space, so the extension has the same Lorentzian signature there. Every coefficient in the global expression is smooth across $r=r_+$ because $\Sigma>0$ and no coefficient contains $\Delta$ in a denominator. It is a smooth Lorentzian extension across $r=r_+$. In this chart $g^{-1}(dr,dr)=\Delta/\Sigma$, so $dr(\sharp_gdr)=g^{-1}(dr,dr)=0$ on $H^+$ by [F9]; the normal is null and tangent there.

Put $A=r^2+a^2$. In the ingoing chart the inverse metric has $g^{vr}=A/\Sigma$, $g^{\widetilde\phi r}=a/\Sigma$, and $g^{rr}=\Delta/\Sigma$. Thus on $H^+$, $\sharp_g(dr)=(A/\Sigma)\partial_v+(a/\Sigma)\partial_{\widetilde\phi}$ by [F9]. The stationary and axial fields remain $\partial_v$ and $\partial_{\widetilde\phi}$, so $\sharp_g(dr)=(A/\Sigma)(T+(a/A)\Phi)$. It follows that the null normal direction is $\chi=T+\Omega_H\Phi$ with $\Omega_H=a/(r_+^2+a^2)$. Equivalently, $\Delta(r_+)=0$ gives $2Mr_+=r_+^2+a^2$, and direct substitution yields $g(\chi,\chi)|_{r_+}=0$. The time orientation also extends explicitly. Write $R:=\partial_r$ in the ingoing product coordinates and set $\overline N:=T-(2Mr/\Sigma)R$. Step 2.1 gives $g(T,R)=1$, $g(R,R)=0$, and $g(T,T)=-(\Delta-a^2q)/\Sigma$. Since $\Sigma=r^2+a^2(1-q)$,
$$g(\overline N,\overline N)=-\frac{\Delta-a^2q+4Mr}{\Sigma}=-\frac{\Sigma+2Mr}{\Sigma}<0$$
on the entire extension, where $r>r_+-\varepsilon>0$. Both product coordinate fields and $\Sigma$ are smooth globally, including the rotation axis, so this is a smooth nowhere-zero timelike field there. On the exterior overlap, $t=v-f(r)$ and $f'=(r^2+a^2)/\Delta$ from step 2.1 imply
$$dt(\overline N)=1+\frac{2Mr(r^2+a^2)}{\Sigma\Delta}>0.$$
Thus $g(N,\overline N)=-dt(\overline N)<0$ by [F2], so the two timelike fields select the same future cone on the overlap. Finally put $A_+:=r_+^2+a^2$ and $\Sigma_+:=r_+^2+a^2(1-q)$. On $H^+$,
$$g(\chi,R)=1-a\Omega_Hq=\frac{\Sigma_+}{A_+}>0.$$
Since $\chi$ is normal to $H^+$ and $T$ is tangent, $g(\chi,T)=0$ there; using $2Mr_+=A_+$ gives
$$g(\chi,\overline N)=-\frac{A_+}{\Sigma_+}\frac{\Sigma_+}{A_+}=-1<0.$$
Therefore the nonzero null generator $\chi$ is future-directed in this proved compatible time orientation, without an extra orientation hypothesis.

From [F1], $g(T,T)=-(1-2Mr/\Sigma)$. It is positive precisely when $r^2-2Mr+a^2\cos^2\theta<0$. The two roots of this quadratic in $r$ are $M\pm\sqrt{M^2-a^2\cos^2\theta}$; because $|a|<M$, they are real, and the upper root is $r_{\mathrm s}(\theta)$. The lower root is at most $r_-$, since $\cos^2\theta\le1$, and $r_-<r_+$; restricting the interval between the roots to the exterior therefore gives exactly $r_+<r<r_{\mathrm s}(\theta)$. At $\theta=0,\pi$ the upper root equals $r_+$. If $a\ne0$ and $0<\theta<\pi$, then $a^2\cos^2\theta<a^2$, so the upper root exceeds $r_+$; if $a=0$, the upper root equals $r_+$ for every $\theta$ and the ergoregion is empty. This proves the stated condition in all allowed cases.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the tangent-bundle smooth structure of the
Lorentzian conventions.

Let $M>0$ and $a\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $|a|<M$, and put
$r_\pm:=M\pm\sqrt{M^2-a^2}$.

Let $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}:=\mathbb R\times(r_+,\infty)\times S^2$ carry the
product smooth structure, where $S^2=\{(x,y,z)\in\mathbb R^3:x^2+y^2+z^2=1\}$
has its usual smooth structure and round metric $\gamma_{S^2}$. Let
$\pi:\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}\to S^2$ be the third projection, let $\xi$ be the
smooth rotation field on $S^2$ generated by $(x,y,z)\mapsto(-y,x,0)$, and put
$\gamma:=\pi^*\gamma_{S^2}$ and
$\xi^\flat:=\pi^*(\gamma_{S^2}(\xi,\cdot))$. Let $t,r$ be the first and
second coordinate functions on $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}$, and let
$\zeta:=z\circ\pi$ be the third Euclidean coordinate on the sphere factor.
Define the global smooth functions

$$\Sigma:=r^2+a^2\zeta^2,\qquad \Delta:=r^2-2Mr+a^2.$$

On a polar chart $0<\theta<\pi$, $\phi\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$, one has
$\zeta=\cos\theta$, $\Sigma=r^2+a^2\cos^2\theta$,
$\gamma=d\theta^2+\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2$, and
$\xi^\flat=\sin^2\theta\,d\phi$.

Define the symmetric covariant $2$-tensor $g$ globally on $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}$
by

$$g=-\left(1-\frac{2Mr}{\Sigma}\right)dt\otimes dt+\frac{\Sigma}{\Delta}\,dr\otimes dr+\Sigma\gamma+\frac{a^2(\Sigma+2Mr)}{\Sigma}\,\xi^\flat\otimes\xi^\flat-\frac{2aMr}{\Sigma}\left(dt\otimes\xi^\flat+\xi^\flat\otimes dt\right).$$

Its Boyer-Lindquist line element on the polar chart is

$$ds^2=-\left(1-\frac{2Mr}{\Sigma}\right)dt^2-\frac{4Mar\sin^2\theta}{\Sigma}\,dt\,d\phi+\frac{\Sigma}{\Delta}\,dr^2+\Sigma\,d\theta^2+\frac{(r^2+a^2)^2-a^2\Delta\sin^2\theta}{\Sigma}\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2.$$

The displayed cross term is $2g_{t\phi}\,dt\,d\phi$. This definition makes
no nondegeneracy or signature claim; Lorentzian signature and a time orientation
are established separately.

For $T=\partial_t$ and $\Phi=\partial_\phi$, the coordinate components are constant, so every term in [F4] vanishes; hence $\mathcal L_Tg=\mathcal L_\Phi g=0$ and both fields are Killing by [F3]. | 2.1: Choose $0<\varepsilon<r_+/2$ and use the extension manifold $\mathbb R_v\times(r_+-\varepsilon,\infty)\times S^2$ with its product smooth structure, round metric $\gamma$, and global axial one-form $\eta$. Fix $r_0>r_+$ and define $f(r)=\int_{r_0}^r (s^2+a^2)/\Delta(s)\,ds$ and $h(r)=\int_{r_0}^r a/\Delta(s)\,ds$ on $(r_+,\infty)$. Their integrands are smooth because $\Delta>0$: repeated use of [F7] gives all derivatives of $\Delta^{-1}$, and [F8] handles the polynomial products. [F6] gives $f,h\in C^1$, and successive differentiation of $f'=(r^2+a^2)/\Delta$ and $h'=a/\Delta$ shows that both primitives are smooth. Set $v=t+f(r)$ and $\widetilde\phi=\phi+h(r)$; globally the sphere coordinate is rotated by the smooth rotation $R_{h(r)}(x,y,z)=(x\cos h-y\sin h,x\sin h+y\cos h,z)$, whose inverse uses $-h(r)$. Repeated application of [F10] makes sine and cosine smooth, and [F8] then makes this rotation smoothly dependent on $r$. Thus this is a smooth coordinate change on the exterior (with coordinate Jacobian determinant $1$), and on an off-axis chart $\eta=\sin^2\theta\,d\widetilde\phi$, while the original $\xi^\flat=\eta-a\sin^2\theta\,\Delta^{-1}dr$. The rotation is generated by $\xi$, so $\eta$ is the standard smooth axial one-form on the new sphere factor. Substitution in [F1], using $\Sigma^2+a^2\sin^2\theta(\Sigma+2Mr)=(r^2+a^2)^2-a^2\Delta\sin^2\theta$, gives the global ingoing expression $g=-(\Delta-a^2|\xi|_\gamma^2)\Sigma^{-1}dv\otimes dv+dv\otimes dr+dr\otimes dv+\Sigma\gamma+a^2(\Sigma+2Mr)\Sigma^{-1}\eta\otimes\eta-2aMr\Sigma^{-1}(dv\otimes\eta+\eta\otimes dv)-a(dr\otimes\eta+\eta\otimes dr)$. Every coefficient is smooth at $r=r_+$ because $\Sigma>0$ there and no coefficient contains $\Delta$ in a denominator. Off the axis the determinant is $-\Sigma^2\sin^2\theta$. Off the axis the angular $2\times2$ block is positive definite; the determinant of its $2\times2$ Schur complement in the $(v,r)$ directions is therefore negative, giving one negative and one positive eigenvalue. At an axis point $\eta=0$ and $\Sigma=r^2+a^2$; the $(v,r)$ block has matrix $\begin{pmatrix}-\Delta/\Sigma&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ of determinant $-1$, and the sphere block is $\Sigma\gamma$, so the extension is Lorentzian there as well. It is consequently a smooth Lorentzian extension across $r=r_+$. In this chart $g^{-1}(dr,dr)=\Delta/\Sigma$, so $dr(\sharp_g dr)=g^{-1}(dr,dr)=0$ on $H^+$ by [F9]; the normal is null and tangent there. | 3.1: Put $A=r^2+a^2$. In the ingoing chart the inverse metric has $g^{vr}=A/\Sigma$, $g^{\widetilde\phi r}=a/\Sigma$, and $g^{rr}=\Delta/\Sigma$. Thus on $H^+$, $\sharp_g(dr)=(A/\Sigma)\partial_v+(a/\Sigma)\partial_{\widetilde\phi}$ by [F9]. The stationary and axial fields remain $\partial_v$ and $\partial_{\widetilde\phi}$, so $\sharp_g(dr)=(A/\Sigma)(T+(a/A)\Phi)$. It follows that the null normal direction is $\chi=T+\Omega_H\Phi$ with $\Omega_H=a/(r_+^2+a^2)$. Equivalently, $\Delta(r_+)=0$ gives $2Mr_+=r_+^2+a^2$, and direct substitution yields $g(\chi,\chi)|_{r_+}=0$. | 4.1: From [F1], $g(T,T)=-(1-2Mr/\Sigma)$. It is positive precisely when $r^2-2Mr+a^2\cos^2\theta<0$. The two roots of this quadratic in $r$ are $M\pm\sqrt{M^2-a^2\cos^2\theta}$; because $|a|<M$, they are real, and the upper root is $r_{\mathrm s}(\theta)$. Restricting to the exterior gives $r_+<r<r_{\mathrm s}(\theta)$. At $\theta=0,\pi$ the upper root equals $r_+$; for $0<\theta<\pi$ it exceeds $r_+$. This proves the stated ergoregion condition.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
For $M>0$, $|a|<M$, and the Kerr exterior tensor datum, define
$T:=\partial_t$, $\Phi:=\xi$, $A:=r^2+a^2$, and $q:=\gamma(\xi,\xi)$.
The global vector field
$$N:=\frac{A^2-a^2\Delta q}{\Sigma\Delta}\,T+\frac{2aMr}{\Sigma\Delta}\,\Phi$$
is smooth; the tensor $g$ is smooth, symmetric, nondegenerate, and has
signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on all of
$\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}=\mathbb R\times(r_+,\infty)\times S^2$; and
$N=-\sharp_g(dt)$ is timelike. Thus $N$ defines a time orientation of this
Lorentzian four-manifold.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $\xi$ be a smooth vector field
on $M$ ([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]). The **Lie
derivative of the metric along $\xi$**, written $\mathcal L_\xi g$, is the
smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field obtained by the flow definition of
[[def-lie-derivative-of-a-tensor-field]] applied to $g$: for the local flow
$\Phi_t$ of $\xi$,

$$\mathcal L_\xi g:=\frac{d}{dt}\Big|_{t=0}\Phi_t^*g .$$

The field $\xi$ is a **Killing field** of $(M,g)$ (an **isometry generator**,
or a **Killing vector**) when

$$\mathcal L_\xi g=0 .$$

The equivalent local characterization

$$\mathcal L_\xi g=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\nabla_a\xi_b+\nabla_b\xi_a=0,$$

where $\nabla$ is the metric-selected connection of $g$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and
$\xi_b:=g_{bc}\xi^c$ is the lowered field, is proved in
[[thm-gr-killing-and-on-shell-matter-identities]] clause (a); the definition
itself asserts neither direction. Whether a given metric has Killing fields is
a property of that metric: neither existence nor uniqueness of a Killing field
is asserted here, and a general metric has none beyond the trivial field
$\xi=0$.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice for the smooth tangent-bundle and time-orientation conventions of the Lorentzian suppliers. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$. A **closed spacelike two-surface** is a nonempty smooth embedded two-manifold $S\subset M$ that is compact without boundary. Let $\iota:S\hookrightarrow M$ be the inclusion and let its induced metric be $q:=\iota^*g$; require $q$ to be positive definite. Its normal bundle is $\mathcal NS=(TS)^\perp$. Work on an open set $U\subseteq S$ carrying a smooth ordered pair of future null normal fields $\ell,k$ with $g(\ell,\ell)=g(k,k)=0$ and $g(\ell,k)=-2$; such pairs exist locally by the preceding lemma. No global pair is part of the definition unless one is explicitly supplied.

For tangent fields $X,Y$ on $U$, define the null second fundamental form, expansion and shear by
$$\chi_\ell(X,Y):=g(\nabla_X\ell,Y),\qquad \theta_\ell:=\operatorname{tr}_q\chi_\ell,\qquad \sigma_\ell:=\chi_\ell-\frac{\theta_\ell}{2}q.$$
Here $\nabla$ is the metric-selected connection; its derivative of a section along $S$ means the pullback connection, equivalently the derivative of any smooth ambient extension along tangent directions. The preceding lemma establishes extension independence, symmetry of $\chi_\ell$, and positive definiteness of the screen metric. A **normal-frame boost** is the change $\ell\mapsto e^f\ell$, $k\mapsto e^{-f}k$ for a smooth real function $f$ on $U$. It leaves $q$ fixed; $\chi_\ell,\theta_\ell,\sigma_\ell$ scale by $e^f$.

A **null geodesic hypersurface congruence from $U$** along the chosen initial normal field $\ell$ is a smooth map $F:U\times J\to M$, where $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ is a nonempty open interval containing $0$, such that $F(p,0)=p$ and $\partial_\lambda F(p,0)=\ell_p$ for every $p\in U$, each curve $\gamma_p(\lambda):=F(p,\lambda)$ is future-directed and null, and its tangent $\ell:=\partial_\lambda F$ obeys the affine geodesic equation
$$D_\lambda\ell=0$$
along every curve $\gamma_p$; here $D_\lambda$ is the covariant derivative along a curve from [[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]. For each $p\in U$, let $J_{\mathrm{reg}}(p)$ be the connected component containing $0$ of the parameter values for which $d(F_\lambda)_p:T_pU\to T_{F(p,\lambda)}M$ is injective and the pullback form $(X,Y)\mapsto g(d(F_\lambda)_pX,d(F_\lambda)_pY)$ is positive definite on $T_pU$. Require, for every $\lambda\in J$, that its variation directions satisfy
$$g_{F(p,\lambda)}\bigl(\ell(p,\lambda),dF_{(p,\lambda)}(X,0)\bigr)=0\qquad(X\in T_pU).$$
Thus its variation directions are orthogonal to $\ell$. For $\lambda\in J_{\mathrm{reg}}(p)$, the map $F$ has rank three locally near $(p,\lambda)$: its two section directions are spacelike and orthogonal to the nonzero null vector $\ell$. Its local image is a null hypersurface, with tangent space $\ell^\perp$ and induced radical $\mathbb R\ell$, as in [[lem-gr-fx-null-normal-plane-and-screen]]. The parameter $\lambda$ is affine. On each section in $J_{\mathrm{reg}}$, the **screen** is $\mathscr S=\ell^\perp/\mathbb R\ell$ with metric $\bar q([X],[Y])=g(X,Y)$; it is the positive two-dimensional quotient, identified isometrically with the tangent plane of that section by projection. The induced form on the full null hypersurface has radical $\mathbb R\ell$ and has no inverse. All traces and inverses in this definition are taken on the screen.

All screen bundles associated with this congruence are understood as bundles over the parameter domain $U\times J$: the notation $\mathscr S_{F(p,\lambda)}$ denotes the branch determined by $(p,\lambda)$, so self-intersections do not identify distinct screen fibers. For each $\lambda\in J$, the screen Jacobi map $A_\lambda:T_pS\to\mathscr S_{F(p,\lambda)}$ sends $X$ to the screen class of the variation field $J_X(\lambda):=dF_{(p,\lambda)}(X,0)$; it is invertible for $\lambda\in J_{\mathrm{reg}}(p)$. A **focal instant** is a positive parameter in $J$ where $A_\lambda$ loses rank; the **first focal instant**, if it exists, is the least such parameter after $0$. Along an affine generator the screen derivative is $\mathcal D_\ell[X]:=[D_\ell X]$; it is independent of the representative, by the preceding lemma. On $J_{\mathrm{reg}}$, the derivative $A_\lambda'$ is taken using $\mathcal D_\ell$, and the **optical endomorphism** is $B_\lambda:=A_\lambda'A_\lambda^{-1}$. Its **optical expansion** is $\theta:=\operatorname{tr}B$, and its **optical shear** is $\sigma:=B-\frac12\theta\,\mathrm{id}_{\mathscr S}$. Since the congruence is normal to a null hypersurface, $B$ is self-adjoint. Its antisymmetric part $\omega:=(B-B^*)/2$, called the twist, therefore vanishes. At $\lambda=0$, $B$ is the endomorphism $q^{-1}\chi_\ell$ and these optical quantities agree with $\theta_\ell,\sigma_\ell$.

No orientation of $M$, $S$, or the screen is required for these constructions. Indeed, if two orthonormal screen frames are related by a real $2\times2$ matrix $O$ with $O^{\mathsf T}O=I_2$, then the endomorphism matrices obey $\widehat B=O^{-1}BO$ and $\widehat\sigma=O^{-1}\sigma O$. The preceding lemma establishes extension independence, symmetry of $\chi_\ell$, and positive definiteness of the screen metric. A **normal-frame boost** is the change $\ell\mapsto e^f\ell$, $k\mapsto e^{-f}k$ for a smooth real function $f$ on $U$. It leaves $q$ fixed; $\chi_\ell,\theta_\ell,\sigma_\ell$ scale by $e^f$.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $I \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be order-convex with at least two elements
([[def-interval]]) and let $f : I \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $I$
([[def-continuity-real]]). Call $G : I \to \mathbb{R}$ a **primitive of $f$ on
$I$** when $G$ is differentiable at every point of $I$ as a function on $I$ with
$G' = f$ there ([[def-derivative]]). Then:

1. **Existence.** Fix $c_0 \in I$. The function
   $$F : I \to \mathbb{R}, \qquad F(x) \;:=\; \int_{c_0}^x f$$
   is defined at every $x \in I$ ([[def-oriented-integral]],
   [[def-the-integral-function]]) and is a primitive of $f$ on $I$.
2. **Uniqueness up to a constant.** If $G_1$ and $G_2$ are primitives of $f$ on
   $I$ then there is a real $k$ with $G_1(x) = G_2(x) + k$ for every $x \in I$.
3. **Evaluation.** If $a, b \in I$ with $a < b$ and $G$ is any primitive of $f$
   on $I$, then
   $$\int_a^b f \;=\; G(b) - G(a) .$$

**The scope is exactly the continuous case, and that is not a limitation of the
proof.** An integrable function need not have a primitive, and a function with a
primitive need not be integrable; this corollary is precisely the intersection
where both fundamental theorems apply, and both witnesses are on the companion
page.

supplier_excerpts.consumer_use: 2.1: Choose $0<\varepsilon<r_+/2$ and use the extension manifold $\mathbb R_v\times(r_+-\varepsilon,\infty)\times S^2$ with its product smooth structure, round metric $\gamma$, and global axial one-form $\eta$. Fix $r_0>r_+$ and define $f(r)=\int_{r_0}^r (s^2+a^2)/\Delta(s)\,ds$ and $h(r)=\int_{r_0}^r a/\Delta(s)\,ds$ on $(r_+,\infty)$. Their integrands are smooth because $\Delta>0$: repeated use of [F7] gives all derivatives of $\Delta^{-1}$, and [F8] handles the polynomial products. [F6] gives $f,h\in C^1$, and successive differentiation of $f'=(r^2+a^2)/\Delta$ and $h'=a/\Delta$ shows that both primitives are smooth. Set $v=t+f(r)$ and $\widetilde\phi=\phi+h(r)$; globally the sphere coordinate is rotated by the smooth rotation $R_{h(r)}(x,y,z)=(x\cos h-y\sin h,x\sin h+y\cos h,z)$, whose inverse uses $-h(r)$. Repeated application of [F10] makes sine and cosine smooth, and [F8] then makes this rotation smoothly dependent on $r$. Thus this is a smooth coordinate change on the exterior (with coordinate Jacobian determinant $1$), and on an off-axis chart $\eta=\sin^2\theta\,d\widetilde\phi$, while the original $\xi^\flat=\eta-a\sin^2\theta\,\Delta^{-1}dr$. The rotation is generated by $\xi$, so $\eta$ is the standard smooth axial one-form on the new sphere factor. Substitution in [F1], using $\Sigma^2+a^2\sin^2\theta(\Sigma+2Mr)=(r^2+a^2)^2-a^2\Delta\sin^2\theta$, gives the global ingoing expression $g=-(\Delta-a^2|\xi|_\gamma^2)\Sigma^{-1}dv\otimes dv+dv\otimes dr+dr\otimes dv+\Sigma\gamma+a^2(\Sigma+2Mr)\Sigma^{-1}\eta\otimes\eta-2aMr\Sigma^{-1}(dv\otimes\eta+\eta\otimes dv)-a(dr\otimes\eta+\eta\otimes dr)$. Every coefficient is smooth at $r=r_+$ because $\Sigma>0$ there and no coefficient contains $\Delta$ in a denominator. Off the axis the determinant is $-\Sigma^2\sin^2\theta$. Off the axis the angular $2\times2$ block is positive definite; the determinant of its $2\times2$ Schur complement in the $(v,r)$ directions is therefore negative, giving one negative and one positive eigenvalue. At an axis point $\eta=0$ and $\Sigma=r^2+a^2$; the $(v,r)$ block has matrix $\begin{pmatrix}-\Delta/\Sigma&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ of determinant $-1$, and the sphere block is $\Sigma\gamma$, so the extension is Lorentzian there as well. It is consequently a smooth Lorentzian extension across $r=r_+$. In this chart $g^{-1}(dr,dr)=\Delta/\Sigma$, so $dr(\sharp_g dr)=g^{-1}(dr,dr)=0$ on $H^+$ by [F9]; the normal is null and tangent there.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). The cotangent space $T_p^*M$ is
the algebraic dual of $T_pM$ ([[def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional]]).

**Musical isomorphisms.** Define the **flat map**

$$\flat_p:T_pM\longrightarrow T_p^*M,\qquad \flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot),$$

so that $\flat_p(v)(w)=g_p(v,w)$; it is $\mathbb R$-linear by bilinearity of
$g_p$. Its kernel is $\{v:g_p(v,w)=0\text{ for all }w\}=\{0\}$ because $g_p$ is
nondegenerate, and $\dim_{\mathbb R}T_pM=\dim_{\mathbb R}T_p^*M=4$ since the
coordinate derivations of a chart form a basis of $T_pM$
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]); hence
$\flat_p$ is a linear isomorphism and has an inverse
$\sharp_p:T_p^*M\to T_pM$.

**Inverse metric.** The **inverse metric** at $p$ is the symmetric bilinear form

$$g_p^{-1}:T_p^*M\times T_p^*M\longrightarrow\mathbb R,\qquad g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta).$$

It is symmetric because $g_p$ is, and it is nondegenerate: if
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta)=0$ for all $\beta$, then $g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\cdot)=0$,
so $\sharp_p\alpha=0$ and hence $\alpha=0$.

**Components in a chart.** Let $(U,x)$ be a smooth chart and
$g_{ab}(q)=g_q(\partial_a|_q,\partial_b|_q)$ the components of $g$; let
$dx^a|_q$ be the differential of the coordinate function $x^a$ at $q$
([[def-differential-of-a-smooth-map]]), so that
$dx^a|_q(\partial_b|_q)=\partial_b|_q(x^a)=\delta^a{}_b$. Define the components
of the inverse metric in this chart by

$$g^{ab}(q):=g_q^{-1}\bigl(dx^a|_q,\,dx^b|_q\bigr),\qquad q\in U,$$

so that $\sharp_q(dx^a|_q)=\sum_bg^{ab}(q)\,\partial_b|_q$; equivalently
$(g^{ab}(q))$ is the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab}(q))$ at every $q$, that is

$$g^{ac}(q)\,g_{cb}(q)=\delta^a{}_b,\qquad g_{ac}(q)g^{cb}(q)=\delta_a{}^b,$$

because $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=dx^a|_q(\partial_c|_q)=\delta^a{}_c$
and also $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=\sum_bg^{ab}(q)g_{bc}(q)$. In
particular $g^{ab}=g^{ba}$. The components $g^{ab}$ depend smoothly on $q$;
this is proved in [[lem-gr-inverse-metric-is-smooth]].

**Raising, lowering and metric trace.** Let $A$ be a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field on an open set $V\subseteq M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). At each $p\in V$ define the
endomorphism

$$A^\sharp_p:T_pM\to T_pM,\qquad A^\sharp_p(v):=\sharp_p\bigl(A_p(v,\cdot)\bigr),$$

characterized by $g_p(A^\sharp_p(v),w)=A_p(v,w)$ for all $w\in T_pM$; it is
self-adjoint for $g_p$ because $A_p$ is symmetric. Its **metric trace** is

$$\operatorname{tr}_g(A)(p):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(A^\sharp_p\bigr)$$

with the trace of an endomorphism as in [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. In a
chart the raised, mixed and doubly raised components are

$$A^{ab}:=g^{ac}g^{bd}A_{cd},\qquad A^a{}_b:=g^{ac}A_{cb},\qquad\text{and}\qquad \operatorname{tr}_g(A)=g^{ab}A_{ab},$$

the last identity obtained by evaluating in a $g_p$-orthonormal basis
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$, where $g_p(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ by
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]] so that
$g^{ab}A_{ab}=\sum_a g^{aa}A_{aa}=-A(e_0,e_0)+A(e_1,e_1)+A(e_2,e_2)+A(e_3,e_3)$,
which is the trace of the endomorphism $v\mapsto\sharp_p(A_p(v,\cdot))$ in that
basis. All these operations are pointwise and depend only on $g$, $A$ and the
duality pairing, not on a chart.

**Conventions.** Raising and lowering apply to one index at a time and preserve
index order; $A_{ab}$, $A^a{}_b$ and $A^{ab}$ denote the same tensor $A$ with
indices positioned by $g$. The musical isomorphisms and the inverse metric are
defined for every smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of this library; no choice
principle is used in this definition, every ingredient being pointwise linear
algebra over $\mathbb R$ together with the pointwise nondegeneracy of $g_p$.
